gaps: Whether the funnel time-to-convert histogram exposes its underlying bin data through the query API (which would let a SQL insight derive p75 from the same server-corrected timestamps the funnel uses) — the issue thread implies not, but the FunnelsQuery schema was not read. Ten minutes in a live project or one read of the funnel_time_to_convert query node would settle it.

The exact funnel conversion-window UNITS. The 14-day default is confirmed and the parameter is funnel_window_interval, but PostHog's docs never list the selectable units, so the spec cannot yet state 'set TTFA to a 1-hour window' with certainty rather than '1 day'.

Whether quantile() actually executes in a HogQL insight. The supported-aggregations page lists it; the ClickHouse-functions and SQL-expressions pages both omit it. One query in a live project decides whether the SQL p75 fallback is real.

Whether PostHog permits migrating a project between US and EU cloud regions after creation. The data-residency page only recommends EU for GDPR and is silent on migration — and Agora sells hosting-region choice, so picking the wrong PostHog region now may be irreversible. Needs PostHog support or the migration docs.

Session replay per-recording price beyond the 5,000 free monthly recordings — the pricing page fetch returned only the free tier, so the cost of the proposed 20%-sampled builder replay exception above 5k recordings is unpriced.

Whether funnel correlation analysis is plan-gated. The correlation doc names no tier and no minimum sample, only that accuracy 'depends on the sample size' — so the first pass's 'cheapest way to test the A8 preflight hypothesis' may carry a plan requirement.

Whether posthog-cli exp schema commands can run non-interactively in CI with POSTHOG_CLI_API_KEY alone, and whether `exp schema status` returns a non-zero exit code on drift. Without a non-zero exit there is no gate at all, and the docs show no CI example.

No competitor's actual measured onboarding telemetry — only their marketing claims. Nothing external validates a 3-minute median as achievable; the target remains internally derived from the dwell-budget sum, now bracketed by competitor claims of 5–15 minutes.

corpus.headline: On the default agent the builder is already near-optimal — 1–2 clicks to hear it talk and 0 clicks to deploy (it ships live) — but the cold-start path is 7 clicks with zero keys and zero typing, and the entire funnel currently emits only 3 analytics events, none of which can distinguish a real test from the canned demo transcript.

findings.claim: TTFA on /agents/agt_default/edit is 2 clicks via the header, or 1 click via 'Hear the opening' — and the first agent line renders 500 ms after the click.
findings.detail: agt_default loads through agentToDraft() fully populated (voice_jenny, channels ['inbound'], numberIds ['pn_02'], persona prompt, balanced stack). The right rail auto-opens at ≥1024px but on the 'simulations' tab (testTab initial state = "simulations"), so hearing the agent costs: click header 'Voice call' (openTest('agent')) → click 'Talk to Aria' (onToggleTalk → toggleTest). SimTranscript's stream effect reveals turn 1 after a 500 ms timer, then 1200 ms per turn (500 + 700), so the 5-turn RAIL_TALK script completes in ~5.3 s. Section 3's 'Hear the opening' button does both in one click: onHearOpening = () => { openTest('agent'); if (!testing) toggleTest() }.
findings.soWhat: Baseline TTFA to instrument = 2 clicks / ~0.5 s to first audio, 0 required fields, 0 credentials, 0 navigations. The one avoidable click is the rail's default tab: landing on 'simulations' hides the Talk button. Test defaulting the rail to Voice call for a live agent and keeping Simulations as the header door.
findings.source: components/wizard/agent-wizard.tsx (testTab init, openTest, toggleTest); components/wizard/test-panel.tsx (TalkTab); components/sim-transcript.tsx (SimTranscript stream)

findings.claim: The Talk surface is not gated by configuration at all — an empty draft with no voice, no prompt and no channel plays the same scripted transcript.
findings.detail: TalkTab's button is disabled only by `talkDisabled` (the first-run 'warming' prop). With EMPTY_DRAFT the greeting is empty so `turns` falls back to the hard-coded RAIL_TALK array ('Hi! Thanks for calling…' / order 4471). toggleTest fires agent_test_started with agent_id 'new' and channel 'unknown'. Nothing in the payload records whether a voice, prompt or greeting existed.
findings.soWhat: Any TTFA metric built on agent_test_started today will count canned-demo plays as agent tests. Add a `configured` boolean (voice != null && systemPrompt.trim() != '') and a `heard_own_greeting` flag to the event before PostHog lands, or the headline metric is unfalsifiable.
findings.source: components/wizard/test-panel.tsx RAIL_TALK + TalkTab; components/wizard/agent-wizard.tsx toggleTest

findings.claim: Cold start to a deployed inbound agent is exactly 7 clicks, 0 keystrokes and 0 API keys.
findings.detail: From /agents/new/edit (EMPTY_DRAFT): (1) 'Browse voices' → (2) 'Use' on a voice row — VoiceBrowser.use() closes the dialog and seedFromVoice() fills voice + name + systemPrompt (defaultPromptFor) + greeting, so section 3 completes for free; (3) 'Inbound' radio card — setChannel seeds config.inbound = { numberIds: [], surfaces: ['phone'] }; (4) phone-number Select trigger → (5) a number option; (6) header 'Deploy' → DeployPreflight; (7) 'Deploy' in the preflight → 900 ms launch burst → publishDeployment. Naming the agent is optional (publish falls back to 'Your agent').
findings.soWhat: 7 clicks / zero credentials is the number to put against Vapi/Retell. The single biggest accelerant already in the code is seedFromVoice: one voice pick satisfies two of the four publish blocks. Protect it and consider extending it (a voice pick could also default the channel).
findings.source: components/wizard/agent-wizard.tsx seedFromVoice + publish; components/wizard/voice-browser.tsx use(); components/wizard/channel-section.tsx setChannel

findings.claim: Only four things block deploy, and none of them is a credential, a model, a region or a test result.
findings.detail: publishBlocks() in lib/wizard-draft.ts returns, in journey order: no voice (step 1), no channel (step 2), inbound with zero surfaces (step 2), inbound+phone with zero numberIds (step 2), empty systemPrompt (step 3), then the batch set (no active run when batch is the sole channel; per-run missing numberId / csvName / schedule fields; prompt {{vars}} not covered by MOCK_CSV_COLUMNS). Models, hosting region, structured outputs, advanced speech, backup providers, failure message and the scenario suite never block. eval-tests states it outright: 'Failing scenarios never block deploy.'
findings.soWhat: The blocked-reason taxonomy for PostHog is fixed and small — 9 distinct reasons. Instrument publishBlocks' first block as a `deploy_blocked{reason, step}` property on every deploy click; that single dimension explains most drop-off between Deploy-clicked and deployment_went_live.
findings.source: lib/wizard-draft.ts publishBlocks / publishBlockReason; components/eval-tests.tsx InfoHint

findings.claim: Deploy is never hard-disabled — it is a soft gate with three different surfaces that can contradict each other.
findings.detail: StepPublish's Deploy button is always clickable ('No hard lock'). publish() re-checks publishBlockReason and toasts on failure. DeployPreflight only swaps its primary for 'Review fixes' when warns exist. Meanwhile the header CTA has five branches in deployCta: Deploy · Redeploy · 'Launch batch calls' · 'Live. No changes' · Redeploy-for-code. The repo's own audit (docs/revamp/AUDIT.md A1) already flags 'Live — no changes' as unreadable as button-vs-state.
findings.soWhat: 'Live. No changes' is a no-op primary: clicking it only toasts 'Already live'. That is a click the funnel will record as intent-to-deploy with no outcome. Either make it a status chip, or fire a distinct `deploy_noop` event so it never pollutes deploy-click counts.
findings.source: components/wizard/agent-wizard.tsx deployCta + publish early-return; components/wizard/step-publish.tsx; docs/revamp/AUDIT.md line 142

findings.claim: On the default agent there is no deploy path at all until the user edits something — the flagship URL cannot demonstrate 'time to deployed agent'.
findings.detail: agt_default has status 'live' in AGENTS, so isLive is true, dirtyCount = 0, deployCta = 'Live. No changes', and publish() returns early with a toast before the preflight can open. It is already answering +1 (628) 555-0188 (pn_02). The genuine deploy funnel only exists from /agents/new/edit or the create dialog.
findings.soWhat: Measure two funnels, not one: 'first test on the provisioned agent' (the belief moment, already ~0 friction) and 'first self-built agent deployed' (7 clicks). Conflating them will make TTFA look artificially perfect.
findings.source: lib/campaign-data.ts AGENTS[0]; components/wizard/agent-wizard.tsx publish()

findings.claim: The rail's 'n of 5 done' counter is not a completion measure — section 4 (Test) is hard-coded done and section 5 only ticks if the agent was already live at page load.
findings.detail: isDone(n) in agent-wizard.tsx: 1 = draft.voice !== null; 2 = channels.length > 0 plus the inbound surface/number check; 3 = systemPrompt.trim().length > 0; 4 = `true` literally; 5 = isLive, which is computed once from existing.status and is not recomputed after an in-session deploy. So a blank draft reads '1 of 5 done' on arrival and a just-deployed new agent never reaches 5 of 5.
findings.soWhat: Do not use this fraction as a funnel metric. Either make 4 real (done once a sim run or a talk test has completed — simSummary is already tracked in state) and 5 reactive to the publish, or stop counting them. Right now the page's only visible progress signal is wrong in both directions.
findings.source: components/wizard/agent-wizard.tsx isDone / rail header counter; components/wizard/types.tsx SECTION_GROUPS

findings.claim: Exactly three analytics events fire anywhere in the builder, and one of them reports a fabricated duration.
findings.detail: grep of track(Events.*) across components/wizard finds only agent-wizard.tsx:870-871 (agent_test_started / agent_test_ended) and channel-configs.tsx:87,89 (deployment_went_live + time_to_live_ms). agent_test_ended sends `duration_sec: 30` as a literal — no timer exists. Events defined in lib/analytics.ts but never fired from the builder include agent_published, test_outcome_selected, stack_preset_changed, agent_created, campaign_created, campaign_launched and phone_number_assigned.
findings.soWhat: The instrumentation surface is a taxonomy, not an implementation. Before PostHog, the minimum viable set is: builder_opened, section_opened, voice_selected, channel_selected, number_linked, deploy_clicked{blocked_reason}, preflight_opened/confirmed/abandoned, agent_test_started/ended with a real timer. Fixing duration_sec is a two-line change (a useRef timestamp in toggleTest).
findings.source: components/wizard/agent-wizard.tsx toggleTest; components/wizard/channel-configs.tsx publishDeployment; lib/analytics.ts Events

findings.claim: time_to_live_ms is currently measured from the first builder mount ever in that browser, not from this session — the headline speed number is wrong for every returning user.
findings.detail: markBuildStart() writes sx:build_start_ts only `if (!localStorage.getItem(BUILD_START_KEY))`. timeToLiveMs() reads and deletes it, so the clock is only reset by a successful deploy. A user who opens the builder on Monday and deploys on Friday reports a four-day time-to-live. The wizard calls markBuildStart() on every mount of the editor route (and the mount effect bails out early only for ?view=list).
findings.soWhat: Stamp per build attempt, not per browser: key the stamp by agent id + a session nonce, expire it (e.g. 2 h idle), and emit both `ms_since_builder_open` and `ms_active_in_builder`. Until then, any TTL chart is unusable for the '<3 minute deploy' claim the taxonomy comments promise.
findings.source: lib/analytics.ts markBuildStart / timeToLiveMs (BUILD_START_KEY); components/wizard/agent-wizard.tsx mount effect

findings.claim: There is exactly one hard page-exit inside the configuration flow, and it is buried three levels deep: Create credential does a full window.location.assign out of a sheet inside an expander.
findings.detail: stack-config.tsx:526, inside CredentialField's Select onValueChange: `if (v === "__create__") { window.location.assign("/project/vendor-credentials"); return }`. The user is inside the ConfigureSlotSheet, which is inside the 'Or Configure models manually' expander, which is inside section 1. It is a full document navigation (not router.push), so React state is destroyed; only the 600 ms-debounced localStorage draft survives, and there is no return-to-builder affordance on the credentials page.
findings.soWhat: This is the highest-value leak to close and to instrument. Either make credential creation an in-sheet form (the AddPhoneNumberSheet already proves the pattern works in-builder) or at minimum fire `credential_page_exit{slot, vendor, agent_id}` before the assign and carry a ?returnTo= back. Agora's managed-key advantage means most users never touch it — which is exactly why the ones who do are a high-intent cohort worth counting.
findings.source: components/wizard/stack-config.tsx line 526 (CredentialField)

findings.claim: Nine further exits leave the builder, but all are soft links in hint copy rather than required steps — the flow itself is genuinely single-page.
findings.detail: hosting-region.tsx:76 → /project/vendor-credentials; channel-section.tsx:148 and :402 → /integrations?tab=channels ('Resources › Deployment Channels', printed twice); step-build.tsx:127 → router.push('/integrations?tab=connectors') for Add Connector (the only way to add a connector); widget-studio.tsx:367 and channel-configs.tsx:378 → /deploy/web-widget; deploy-preflight.tsx:312 → /calls, inside the deploy dialog; CodeConfigure → docs.agora.io; agent-wizard.tsx:784 → /agents/new/edit; editor-client onCreateNew → window.location.assign('/agents/new/edit?blank=1'). Adding a phone number does NOT exit — AddPhoneNumberSheet and SipQuickConnect run inline.
findings.soWhat: Only two of these are on a required path: Add Connector (router.push, unavoidable today) and Create credential. Everything else is optional depth. Instrument all of them as `builder_exit{target, section}` — a spike on any optional link is a sign the hint copy is being read as an instruction.
findings.source: components/wizard/hosting-region.tsx; channel-section.tsx; step-build.tsx; widget-studio.tsx; channel-configs.tsx; deploy-preflight.tsx

findings.claim: Deploying force-navigates the user out of the builder to /monitor — the funnel's last step is an exit, and only the Code/SDK path is exempt.
findings.detail: publishDeployment() ends with router.push('/monitor?' + params) unless `stay` is true, which agent-wizard sets only when primaryChannel === 'code'. For inbound and batch the user lands on Monitor with a success toast; the draft slot is cleared via clearDraft(). StepPublish's fine print announces this ('Opens Monitor.').
findings.soWhat: The post-deploy moment is where 'confidence in production' has to be built, and today it happens on a different page with no agent context carried beyond query params. Either keep the user in the builder with a live-status panel, or make /monitor?deployed= a real first-call-watch view. Instrument `first_real_call_received` against deployment_went_live — that gap is the true 'is it working in production?' metric.
findings.source: components/wizard/channel-configs.tsx publishDeployment; components/wizard/step-publish.tsx copy

findings.claim: Almost every field already has a sensible default; only six things are genuinely empty on a new draft, and picking a voice kills two of them.
findings.detail: Pre-filled: stack = balanced (750 ms, $0.10/min, all Agora-managed), language English, DEFAULT_ADVANCED (turn detection balanced/threshold 50, interrupt 160 ms, end-of-speech silence 640 ms, history 20), DEFAULT_ANALYSIS (transcribe on, record on, one 'Call Outcome' data point), DEFAULT_CALL_BEHAVIOR (endCall, endOfConversation, voicemail detection, silence hang-up at 120 s, max duration 300 s, ring 30 s, transfer OFF, 1000 ms pacing), hosting Automatic, credential mode 'managed' for asr/llm/tts. Empty on EMPTY_DRAFT: name, voice, channels, systemPrompt, greeting, failureMessage — and seedFromVoice fills name, systemPrompt and greeting the moment a voice is picked.
findings.soWhat: The defaults story is already a competitive advantage; the gap is that nothing tells the user how little is left. A one-line 'Ready except: a voice and a number' banner (publishBlocks already computes it) would turn an implicit advantage into a visible one, and gives a clean `blocks_remaining` counter to chart over session time.
findings.source: lib/wizard-draft.ts EMPTY_DRAFT / DEFAULT_ADVANCED / DEFAULT_ANALYSIS / DEFAULT_CALL_BEHAVIOR; lib/campaign-data.ts STACK_PRESETS

findings.claim: Two defaults guarantee a red row in the auto-generated test suite, and one default contradicts the new-agent AI-disclosure rule.
findings.detail: DEFAULT_CALL_BEHAVIOR.transfer = false, so the 'Asks for a human' scenario's failsBecause() fires for any inbound or batch agent — the generated suite always opens with at least one failure. Separately, EMPTY_DRAFT sets opening.disclose = true (EU AI Act Art. 50), but agentToDraft() never writes an `opening` object, so every existing agent — including the flagship agt_default — falls back to DEFAULT_OPENING with disclose = false.
findings.soWhat: The guaranteed-fail row is arguably good (it teaches the control) but it will depress any 'scenarios passed' metric and shows up in the preflight's sim echo. Decide deliberately. The disclosure asymmetry means the demo agent ships non-compliant while a blank draft ships compliant — worth a product call before it reaches a customer demo.
findings.source: components/wizard/test-section.tsx SCENARIO_SEEDS.failsBecause; lib/wizard-draft.ts DEFAULT_OPENING vs EMPTY_DRAFT vs agentToDraft

findings.claim: The deploy pre-flight is the funnel's last gate, is fully untracked, and adds ~1.1 s of theatre before its verdict lands.
findings.detail: DeployPreflight builds 6 rows for a simple inbound agent (Deployment, Prompt, Voice, Models, Hosting, Outputs) with a 140 ms stagger; settleMs = rows.length * 140 + 250 = 1090 ms before the verdict paragraph fades in (skipped under prefers-reduced-motion). The confirm button is armed immediately when allGo, so the delay is cosmetic — but every Fix button, 'Talk to it first', 'Not yet' and the sim-verdict link emit nothing.
findings.soWhat: Add preflight_opened{rows, warns, all_go, sims_run}, preflight_fix_clicked{row_id}, preflight_talk_first, preflight_abandoned and preflight_confirmed. This is where deploy intent converts or dies; without it you cannot tell a blocked deploy from a cold-feet deploy.
findings.source: components/wizard/deploy-preflight.tsx buildRows / settleMs / footer buttons

findings.claim: The right rail already ships a live 'Session statistics' panel that models latency and cost per slot — the honest scaffolding for a real TTFA/latency readout.
findings.detail: test-panel.tsx SessionStatistics renders LLM/ASR/TTS vendor + per-hop ms from stackLatencyDetail(), then Avg e2e latency, Avg LLM TTFT (computed as round(llmMs * 0.18)) and Avg cost $/min, footed with 'Wireframe estimates.' The underlying model is in lib/campaign-data.ts: per-model latencyMs/costPerMin plus PIPELINE_OVERHEAD_MS = 120 and AGORA_RATE_PER_MIN = 0.10. lib/session-trace.ts defines LATENCY_TARGET_MS = 1000 as the developer-facing budget.
findings.soWhat: When real telemetry arrives, swap the estimate for measured p50/p95 from the last test call in this same panel — the layout, the labels and the target constant already exist. That turns the model-tier slider from a promise into evidence, which is the cheapest available 'confidence in production' win.
findings.source: components/wizard/test-panel.tsx SessionStatistics; lib/campaign-data.ts stackCost / stackLatencyDetail; lib/session-trace.ts LATENCY_TARGET_MS

findings.claim: Every draft write in the builder funnels through one `update(patch)` callback — a single throttled hook there yields per-field engagement for free.
findings.detail: agent-wizard.tsx defines `const update = React.useCallback((patch: Partial<AgentDraft>) => { dirty.current = true; setSaveState('saving'); setDraft(d => ({...d, ...patch})) }, [])` and passes it down to VoiceSection, ChannelSection, SectionPrompt, SectionOpening, SectionKnowledgeTools, DeploySection and CampaignsCard via StepProps. Autosave is a 600 ms useDebouncedEffect on [draft].
findings.soWhat: Instrument Object.keys(patch) here, throttled to once per key per 10 s, to get time-to-first-edit-per-field and dwell per section without touching 12 components. Pair it with openRow(n) (the single funnel for rail clicks, ⌘K events, deep links and every 'Fix this' jump) for section-level dwell.
findings.source: components/wizard/agent-wizard.tsx update() and openRow(); components/wizard/types.tsx StepProps; hooks/use-debounced-effect.ts

findings.claim: How long a user can sit on a task is already bounded by localStorage, not by session — the builder resumes unsaved edits indefinitely, per agent.
findings.detail: saveDraft/restoreDraft key on `sx:agent_draft` for new drafts and `sx:agent_draft:<id>` for edits; hasDraft/clearDraft manage them. Edit mode toasts 'Resuming unsaved edits' with a Discard action; new-agent mode toasts 'Draft restored — picked up at {STEP_TITLES[at-1]}'. Collapse state persists at `sx:wizard_collapsed:<id|new>`, rail-closed at `sx:wizard_rail_closed`, panel width at `sx:test_panel_w`. Nothing expires.
findings.soWhat: 'How long can a user sit on a task' is answerable today from the difference between build_start_ts and the deploy, but only if that stamp is fixed (finding 9). Add a `draft_resumed{age_ms, resume_step}` event on the restore branches — it is the cheapest read on whether multi-session builds are common, which decides whether TTFA should be measured per session or per agent.
findings.source: lib/wizard-draft.ts saveDraft/restoreDraft/hasDraft; components/wizard/agent-wizard.tsx mount effect restore branches

findings.claim: The batch path is materially more expensive than inbound and is where the publish blocks actually bite.
findings.detail: Batch requires: caller-ID number in Deployment (2 clicks), then Go Live → CampaignsCard 'New run' → per-run name, numberId (inherited from the agent caller ID), CSV upload (mocked to contacts.csv / 248 rows / columns name, account, balance, due_date, phone), optional schedule. publishBlocks adds one blocker per run for a missing number, a missing CSV, an incomplete schedule, and one per uncovered {{var}} — and campaignMissingVars treats every referenced variable as missing while there is no CSV.
findings.soWhat: Report TTFA/TTD split by channel. A single 'time to deploy' number will be dominated by whichever channel mix the cohort picks. The batch pre-flight also carries the only money projection in the product (contacts × ~2 min × $/min) — that estimate view is worth its own event.
findings.source: lib/wizard-draft.ts publishBlocks batch branch + campaignMissingVars + MOCK_CSV_COLUMNS/MOCK_CSV_ROWS; components/wizard/campaigns-card.tsx

findings.claim: PostHog is already live in the production Agora Console — posthog-js 1.383.1, a first-party observability facade, a same-origin /ingest reverse proxy in vercel.json, and documented ops runbooks. The telemetry does not need to be 'planned for later'; it needs to be conformed to.
findings.detail: ng-console's package.json pins `posthog-js: ^1.383.1`. `vercel.json` rewrites `/ingest/static/*` → us-assets.i.posthog.com and `/ingest/*` → us.i.posthog.com to survive ad-blockers. `docs/observability/operations.md` names the project (`ng-console`), the env vars (VITE_POSTHOG_KEY / VITE_POSTHOG_HOST / VITE_POSTHOG_UI_HOST) and the Vercel host override. MAINTAINERS.md line 11 names PostHog project `ng-console` as an owned dependency. studio_x_2 by contrast has zero analytics deps — `lib/analytics.ts` only writes to console and a `__SX_EVENTS__` window buffer.
findings.soWhat: Stop designing a greenfield taxonomy. The redesign's instrumentation must be written against `src/lib/observability/facade.ts`, or it will not ship. Budget the migration as 'conform to an existing contract', not 'add analytics'.
findings.source: ng-console: package.json:56, vercel.json:5-13, docs/observability/operations.md, MAINTAINERS.md:11

findings.claim: The three open PostHog questions from pass one are already answered in shipped code: autocapture ON, manual pageviews, session replay OFF at init.
findings.detail: `src/lib/observability/posthog-client.ts` calls `posthog.init(key, { api_host, autocapture: true, capture_pageview: false, disable_session_recording: true, ui_host })`. So the answer is 'both' on autocapture-vs-explicit (autocapture runs alongside explicit `capture`), pageviews are hand-fired via `trackPassive('page_viewed', routeContext)` from console-shell.tsx:1293, and the replay-on-a-page-that-renders-API-keys risk is already closed by policy — `sentry.replayEnabled` is typed as the literal `false` in config.ts, so it cannot be turned on by config either.
findings.soWhat: Drop session replay from the decision list for the agent builder; it is disabled product-wide. Do keep an explicit event for every step of the TTFA/TTFD funnel — PostHog's own docs say autocapture 'only works on the frontend' and breaks when button text changes, which is guaranteed in a design revamp.
findings.source: ng-console src/lib/observability/posthog-client.ts:8-16, config.ts (sentry.replayEnabled: false); PostHog docs

findings.claim: Identity is already solved and is *not* anonymous: the console identifies on `accountUid ?? userId` and registers the company `cid` as a PostHog group — and it blocks the entire app from rendering until identify() has resolved.
findings.detail: `facade.ts` identify() calls `posthog.identify(distinctId, sanitized(identity))` then `posthog.group('cid', cid)`. `AuthenticatedObservabilityGate` returns `null` — rendering nothing — until `identifiedIdentity === identity`, so no event can ever fire before identity is attached. That is the opposite of studio_x_2's `lib/analytics.ts`, which has no user id anywhere.
findings.soWhat: Every builder funnel can be computed per-company, not just per-person — which is what a B2B 'how fast is our platform' claim actually needs. But see the cost finding: it also means 100% of console events are identified events.
findings.source: ng-console src/lib/observability/facade.ts:131-152, src/components/providers/authenticated-observability-gate.tsx:30-40

findings.claim: A 48-key camelCase property allowlist silently discards any property not on it — and every property name in both studio_x_2's event set and the existing KPI plan would be dropped on arrival.
findings.detail: `sanitize.ts` runs `POSTHOG_PROPERTY_ALLOWLIST` (48 keys: accountUid, actionKind, appId, cid, commandStep, durationMs, entryPoint, intent, operation, promptBucket, result, route, scenario, surface, trigger …) over every event and drops unknown keys with no warning. Not on it: `agentId`, `agent_id`, `channel`, `duration_sec`, `preset`, `vendor`, `component`, `credentialMode`, `agentState`, `blockingCount`, `passCount`, `scenarioCount`, `voice`, `mode`. studio_x_2's `track(Events.agent_test_started, { channel, agent_id })` would arrive as an event with no properties at all.
findings.soWhat: Before writing a single new builder event, extend sanitize.ts with the builder's dimension names — or rename every builder property onto existing allowlist keys (e.g. use `scenario`, `operation`, `intent`, `durationMs`, `surface`). Otherwise the funnel will look instrumented and be un-sliceable.
findings.source: ng-console src/lib/observability/sanitize.ts:3-52

findings.claim: Three agent-builder events already fire in the live console today and all of them lose their entire payload to that allowlist — a live, checkable defect in the exact Opening section the redesign rebuilt.
findings.detail: `agent-opening-section.tsx` fires `trackPassive('caller_first_selected', { agentId })` (line 114), `trackPassive('ai_disclosure_enabled', { agentId })` (line 129) and `trackPassive('greeting_previewed', { agentId, seconds })` (line 186). Neither `agentId` nor `seconds` is on the allowlist, so all three land in PostHog as bare counts with no agent and no duration. `greeting_previewed` is the event the existing KPI doc proposes to use as the §3 completion signal.
findings.soWhat: Fix this first — it is a one-line allowlist change that retroactively makes an already-firing event usable, and it is the cheapest possible proof that the telemetry plan is real. It also means any 'greeting_previewed' baseline pulled today is uncorrelatable to an agent.
findings.source: ng-console src/components/console/agent-opening-section.tsx:114,129,186 vs src/lib/observability/sanitize.ts

findings.claim: The console's event vocabulary is a closed TypeScript union, and `agent_publish` is already one of its operations — so the terminal event of the time-to-deploy funnel is already instrumented in production with a server-anchored duration.
findings.detail: `types.ts` defines `PassiveEventName` (15 names) and `ProductOperation` (32 names, including `agent_create`, `agent_publish`, `agent_update`, `agent_deployment_status_update`). `use-agents-query.ts` wraps the real mutations: `useCreateAgentMutation` → operation `agent_create` (line 153), `usePublishAgentMutation` → `agent_publish` (line 203). `observeOperation` emits `operation_started`, then `operation_succeeded` with `durationMs = round(performance.now() - startedAt)`, or `operation_failed` with `errorStage`/`errorCode`/`httpStatus`/`retryable`.
findings.soWhat: TTFD's end marker exists and is measured. What is missing is only the *start* marker — there is no `agent_builder_opened` / first-edit event. Add one passive event (and one union member) and the whole deploy clock becomes queryable against real production traffic today, before the redesign ships.
findings.source: ng-console src/lib/observability/types.ts:73-140, src/lib/agents/use-agents-query.ts:144-333, facade.ts:173-223

findings.claim: `posthog-js` may be imported from exactly one file in the whole repo, and a test enforces it — so no instrumentation ported from studio_x_2 can call PostHog directly.
findings.detail: `src/lib/observability/sdk-import-guard.ts` defines `ALLOWED_SDK_IMPORT_FILES` with `'posthog-js': new Set(['src/lib/observability/posthog-client.ts'])` and `findDisallowedSdkImports()` scans sources for both static and dynamic imports. CONTRIBUTING.md:36 states the rule in prose ('Keep Sentry/PostHog imports inside src/lib/observability/').
findings.soWhat: Design the builder's telemetry as a thin `useObservability()` call per handler, not as a `track()` helper of its own. Porting studio_x_2's `lib/analytics.ts` wholesale will fail CI.
findings.source: ng-console src/lib/observability/sdk-import-guard.ts, CONTRIBUTING.md:36

findings.claim: The console auto-classifies any agora.io email as internal traffic — so the design team dogfooding the builder will never appear in the external funnel, and the internal/test split is the only honest way to read a TTFA number.
findings.detail: `identity.ts` has `DEFAULT_INTERNAL_EMAIL_DOMAINS = ['agora.io']` and resolves `trafficType` to internal/test/external/unclassified with a `userClassificationSource` recorded alongside. Critically, `AuthenticatedObservabilityGate` calls `normalizeObservabilityIdentity(user, { environment })` and passes *no* `classifyNonProductionAsTest` and no allowlists — so preview and local deployments fall through to `authenticated_identity` and are counted as **external**, not test.
findings.soWhat: Two actions: (1) every builder funnel must filter `trafficType = external`, or internal dogfooding will flatter the median; (2) pass `classifyNonProductionAsTest: true` at the gate before the redesign goes on a Vercel preview, or preview traffic pollutes the production TTFA baseline.
findings.source: ng-console src/lib/observability/identity.ts:11,75-100; authenticated-observability-gate.tsx:19-25

findings.claim: The click delta the owner will ask for: cold start to a published agent is 4 clicks in the live console versus 7 in the redesign — but the live console's path forces the user to write a system prompt, and the redesign's does not. The redesign is more clicks and less work.
findings.detail: ng-console: click 'Create agent' (name pre-filled 'My Agent', Blank pre-selected at `selectedTemplateId = null`), click 'Create Agent' → `handleCreateAgentFromModal` needs only `activeWorkspaceApp.projectId` and posts `properties: {}`; then click Publish, click Publish in the dialog = 4 clicks. But `validateAgentDetailDraft` returns `system-prompt-required` for an empty prompt, and no default system prompt exists anywhere in `src/lib/agents` — so publish is impossible without free-text typing. studio_x_2's 7-click path types nothing.
findings.soWhat: Frame the speed claim as 'zero keystrokes and zero credential decisions', not 'fewer clicks'. A raw click count makes the redesign look slower. If the 7 clicks matter, the place to cut is the deploy confirmation surfaces, not the configuration.
findings.source: ng-console src/components/console/agents-page.tsx:367-398, console-shell.tsx:2227-2252, agent-detail-authoring-rules.ts:44-48, agent-validation.ts:60-62

findings.claim: The blank-agent fast path in the live console creates a GENERAL_AGENT, not a CALL_AGENT — so the fastest click path there does not produce a telephony agent at all.
findings.detail: `handleCreateAgentFromModal` sets `agentType: input.templateId ? 'CALL_AGENT' : 'GENERAL_AGENT'`, and the create dialog pre-selects Blank (`selectedTemplateId` initialises to `null`). A user who accepts every default in the live console gets an agent of the wrong type for the inbound-phone journey and must restart or switch templates.
findings.soWhat: This is a clean, demonstrable win for the redesign's default-agent story and belongs in the owner's comparison. It also means any 'time to deployed inbound agent' measured on the live console must exclude the blank path, or it will measure a dead end.
findings.source: ng-console src/components/console/console-shell.tsx:2237-2242; agents-page.tsx:369-371

findings.claim: The live console gates the test call on five configuration checks plus a saved-agent requirement, and fails silently when the sixth is unmet — the single largest TTFA difference versus the redesign's ungated Talk surface.
findings.detail: `agent-detail-page.tsx` `handleStartPreview` returns early on, in order: no `savedPreview && builder` (a **silent no-op** — no error, no state change, line 285-287), missing system prompt, `mllm-credentials-missing`, `validateAgentModelConfiguration` first issue, `asrCredentialsMissing`, `ttsCredentialsMissing`. `savedPreview.pipelineId` is required to join, so an unsaved draft cannot be tested at all.
findings.soWhat: This is the concrete mechanism behind the speed claim — and the silent no-op is a TTFA failure that emits no telemetry whatsoever. Whatever the redesign ships, instrument the *refusal*: an `operation_failed`-shaped event on every early return in this function is the cheapest way to learn why users never hear their agent.
findings.source: ng-console src/components/console/agent-detail-page.tsx:284-368

findings.claim: The live console reveals publish blockers one at a time, and re-runs the check inside the dialog so a failure closes the dialog and throws the user back to a toast.
findings.detail: `validateAgentDetailDraft` is a chain of early returns ending in `[issue]` or `issues[0]` — it can never return more than one issue. `handleDetailPublish` toasts the first issue and refuses to open the dialog; `handleDetailPublishConfirm` re-runs the same check and, on failure, calls `setDetailPublishOpen(false)` then `toast.error(...)` — the dialog vanishes mid-action. N blockers therefore cost N publish attempts.
findings.soWhat: studio_x_2's pre-flight listing all blockers at once is a real, defensible improvement — quantify it as 'N attempts collapsed to 1'. And the redesign's pre-flight should never close itself on failure; the live console's dialog-dismiss is the anti-pattern to name in the brief.
findings.source: ng-console src/features/agents/agent-detail-authoring/agent-detail-authoring-rules.ts:29-79; console-shell.tsx:2631-2671

findings.claim: Four of the twelve `?focus=` deep-link targets resolve to nothing in studio_x_2, and the failure is an 8-second silent spin — `backup-providers` even opens a Configure sheet and then abandons the user inside it.
findings.detail: `agent-wizard.tsx:518-521` maps 12 keys. Anchors that exist: `greeting` (section-opening.tsx:104), `turn-taking` and `listening` (via `SectionRow focusId`), `voice-recommended` and `voice-compare` (voice-browser.tsx:195,262), plus `prompt` → `#wz-3-prompt` and `voice` → `#wz-1-voice` by id fallback. Missing entirely: `opening`, `backup-providers`, `deployment` (ids are wz-2-pick/-inbound/-batch…), `test` (wz-4-sims/-review), `golive` (wz-5-kb/-mcp). The retry loop is `tries++ < 40` at 200 ms = 8 s, then it stops with no fallback to `#wizard-step-N` and no console warning. For `backup-providers` `openDoor()` still fires at try 2, expanding 'Configure models manually' and clicking the STT sheet 350 ms later.
findings.soWhat: Fix by adding `data-design-focus` to the five missing rows, and add a last-resort fallback to `document.getElementById('wizard-step-' + n)` so a review link always lands in the right section. Until then any design-review funnel keyed on focus links has four silently dead entry points.
findings.source: studio_x_2 components/wizard/agent-wizard.tsx:517-551; grep of data-design-focus and id="wz-*" across components/wizard

findings.claim: TTFA is not a constant click count per user: one click on the rail's close button writes a localStorage flag that permanently changes the shortest path for that browser, on every agent, forever.
findings.detail: `agent-wizard.tsx:163-179` — the rail auto-opens only `if (window.matchMedia('(min-width: 1024px)').matches)` and only when `localStorage[RAIL_CLOSED_KEY] !== '1'`. `setRailOpen(false)` writes that flag; reopening clears it. The panel width is separately persisted under its own key with MIN_W/MAX_W clamping (test-panel.tsx:111-122).
findings.soWhat: Any TTFA measured as 'clicks' is wrong for returning users. Capture the rail's open/closed state as a property on the test-start event (`surface: 'rail' | 'header' | 'opening'`) so the two populations can be separated — otherwise the p75 will drift upward for no product reason.
findings.source: studio_x_2 components/wizard/agent-wizard.tsx:163-179; components/wizard/test-panel.tsx:107-122

findings.claim: On mobile the two-click TTFA does not exist: the builder header is a single non-wrapping 64px flex row carrying five controls with `shrink-0`, and the mobile sticky strip that replaces it has step chips and Deploy but no test door at all.
findings.detail: `agent-wizard.tsx:957` — `sticky top-12 h-16 flex items-center gap-4 px-5`, with the actions group `flex shrink-0 items-center gap-2` holding More, the config icon, 'Run test scenarios', 'Voice call' and Deploy. No `flex-wrap`, no `overflow-x-auto`, no `lg:` visibility rules. The lg:hidden strip at line 1048 renders chips 1–5, a truncated status line and a single Deploy button. `TestPanel` falls back to a Sheet below 1024 (its own `useBelowLg` at max-width 1023, deliberately not the 768 `useIsMobile`) and is never auto-opened. AUDIT.md:229 records the builder at 390 px as one ~5,000 px column with the rail pushed below, and line 241 says 'mobile layouts break at the header'.
findings.soWhat: Either add a Voice-call control to the mobile sticky strip, or accept that mobile TTFA runs only through 'Hear the opening' inside section 3 — and measure the two viewports as separate funnels. Do not quote one TTFA number across both.
findings.source: studio_x_2 components/wizard/agent-wizard.tsx:957-1077, components/wizard/test-panel.tsx:23-35, docs/revamp/AUDIT.md:229,241

findings.claim: `agent_test_started` already fires with zero user action — the `autoTalk` path starts a test 150 ms after mount — which would make a naive TTFA read as ~0 for every user who arrives that way.
findings.detail: `agent-wizard.tsx:186-190`: `if (autoTalk) window.setTimeout(() => { openTest('agent'); if (!testing) toggleTest() }, 150)`, and `toggleTest` (line 868-873) fires `Events.agent_test_started`. `autoTalk` is set from the agents page (`app/(dashboard)/agents/page.tsx:602,760`) and only for `builderId === 'agt_default'` — i.e. the flagship demo URL.
findings.soWhat: Add a `trigger: 'auto' | 'header' | 'opening' | 'section'` property to the test-start event (note: `trigger` is already on the console's allowlist, so it survives sanitisation) and exclude `auto` from TTFA. Otherwise the headline speed metric is generated by a setTimeout, not a user.
findings.source: studio_x_2 components/wizard/agent-wizard.tsx:186-190,868-873; app/(dashboard)/agents/page.tsx:602,760

findings.claim: Resolve the `agent_test_ended` question by copying the idiom the live console already ships: an unmount cleanup that stops the preview. studio_x_2 has no such cleanup, and rail-close is a separate code path from the toggle.
findings.detail: `setRailOpen(false)` closes the rail without touching `testing`, and `toggleTest` is the only caller of `agent_test_ended`; there is no unmount handler and no `beforeunload`, so a user who closes the rail, folds the section or navigates leaves the session open forever. ng-console's `agent-detail-page.tsx:388-392` does `useEffect(() => () => { void livePreview.stopPreview() }, [livePreview.stopPreview, resolvedAgentId])` — a single cleanup keyed on the agent id.
findings.soWhat: Decision: fire `agent_test_ended` from a `useEffect` cleanup in the component that owns `testing`, with a real elapsed time, plus a `reason: 'toggle' | 'rail_closed' | 'unmount' | 'navigated'`. That eliminates the orphan tail without inventing a new lifecycle.
findings.source: studio_x_2 components/wizard/agent-wizard.tsx:172-179,868-873; ng-console src/components/console/agent-detail-page.tsx:388-392

findings.claim: A moderated 5-user run will NOT give the wall-clock baseline pass one asked for — five users is a qualitative sample, and a quotable time-on-task benchmark needs 20–40+ participants.
findings.detail: The Nielsen–Landauer result is that five users surface roughly 85% of usability *problems* — a formative, problem-finding claim. For quantitative metrics (task-success rate, time-on-task, SUS) the confidence interval at n=5 is enormous; published guidance puts benchmark-grade quantitative work at 20–40 participants, and 30–50+ for numbers you intend to track over time or quote externally.
findings.soWhat: Split the plan: run 5 users to find what makes people hesitate in the 7-click path (cheap, this sprint), and get the wall-clock number from PostHog once the funnel is instrumented — the production population is the only sample large enough to quote. Do not put a 5-user median in front of the owner as 'our TTFA'.
findings.source: Nielsen Norman Group / Nielsen-Landauer, as summarised in current UX-benchmarking guidance

findings.claim: PostHog's funnel conversion window defaults to 14 days — for an in-session TTFA funnel that default will report success for users who came back a week later.
findings.detail: A PostHog funnel is defined by steps, a conversion window (default 14 days), and an order mode (ordered / strict / any order). PostHog's own guidance is to pin the window explicitly: 'a signup→paid funnel might be 30 days; an in-session funnel, 30 minutes.'
findings.soWhat: When the TTFA and TTFD funnels are created, set the conversion window to 30 minutes (TTFA) and 24 hours (TTFD) and use **strict** order for TTFA so an intervening deploy does not count. Write this into the dashboard spec, not just the event spec — the window is where a speed metric quietly becomes a retention metric.
findings.source: PostHog funnels documentation

findings.claim: Because identify() runs before the app renders, 100% of console events are identified events — which PostHog bills at roughly 4–5x the anonymous rate — and the `cid` group already commits the project to the paid Group Analytics add-on.
findings.detail: Reported 2026 rates: anonymous analytics events from about $0.00005 each, identified events from about $0.000198–$0.000248 each — up to ~4x on the same traffic (a 5M-event month quoted at ~$153 anonymous vs ~$610 fully identified). Group Analytics is a separate paid add-on with its own per-event rate, capped at five group types per project; ng-console already uses one (`cid`).
findings.soWhat: An event-per-keystroke design is financially real here. Throttle the per-field engagement hook (pass one's `update(patch)` idea) to one event per field per session rather than per change, and keep the builder's event count to the ~10 funnel milestones plus the existing operation events.
findings.source: PostHog pricing teardowns and add-on pages, 2026

findings.claim: The competitor time-to-first-agent numbers in the public record run from ~2 minutes to 30 minutes, which brackets where a defensible Agora claim has to land.
findings.detail: Developer reports summarised in 2026 comparison write-ups put a working ElevenLabs dashboard agent at 15–30 minutes when you already have an LLM endpoint. At the fast end, xAI's Voice Agent Builder (beta, 1 July 2026) is marketed as shipping a production voice agent on Grok Voice in about two minutes at $0.05/min. No Vapi or Retell first-party 'under 5 minutes' claim surfaced.
findings.soWhat: The existing KPI doc's ≤3 min median / ≤6 min p75 TTFA target sits credibly inside this band and below the ElevenLabs field report — so the target is defensible, but only once measured. Also: nobody in this set publishes a verified median, which means a *measured, sourced* Agora number is itself a marketing asset.
findings.source: Third-party 2026 voice-agent comparisons (StackBriefly, Retell blog, andrew.ooo); no first-party vendor claim found

findings.claim: Dirty-state handling differs in a way that changes 'how long can a user sit on a task': the live console throws a browser 'Leave site?' dialog, the redesign never does.
findings.detail: `AgentDetailNavigationGuard` uses TanStack `useBlocker` with `enableBeforeUnload: () => view.kind === 'ready' && (persistence.kind !== 'clean' || operation !== 'idle')` plus an async `shouldBlockFn` that toasts and blocks in-app navigation. Autosave debounce is `AUTOSAVE_DELAY_MS = 800` and the 'Saved' chip is visible for `SAVED_STATUS_VISIBLE_MS = 3000`. studio_x_2 debounces at 600 ms into localStorage per agent, with no blocker and no beforeunload.
findings.soWhat: The redesign's answer to 'how long can a user sit on a task' is 'indefinitely, per browser' and that is the right answer — but it means a session-based duration metric will have long tails from resumed drafts. Stamp a `builder_session_id` at mount and measure TTFA within a session, not per agent.
findings.source: ng-console src/features/agents/agent-detail-authoring/agent-detail-navigation-guard.tsx:16-35, use-agent-detail-save-status.ts:11, agent-detail-authoring-session.ts:196

findings.claim: The live console's test surface is scripted too — its mock timings are 260/220/760/260 ms — so the redesign's 500 ms first line is not a fabrication relative to a real baseline; neither product has one.
findings.detail: `agent-preview-surface.tsx` defines `CONNECT_DELAY_MS = 260`, `FIRST_TURN_DELAY_MS = 220`, `TURN_DURATION_MS = 760`, `LISTENING_GAP_MS = 260`, used whenever no `livePreview` prop is supplied. When `livePreview` *is* supplied (the agent-detail route does supply it) the surface joins a real session, and `usePreviewAudioDevices` calls `navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia({ audio: true })` — an OS permission prompt that no click count captures and that can add seconds or fail outright.

`docs/design/agent-builder-kpis.md` and `docs/design/agent-builder-migration-brief.md` are untracked in ng-console and appear to be another pass's output rather than shipped repo truth.
