gaps: Still no voice-AI-specific study of pre-launch hesitation. DORA's trust distribution (24% high trust / 30% low) is the best available proxy and it is about software engineers generally, not people putting an agent on a phone number. The first pass's recommendation — 5–8 moderated sessions on the Go Live screen — remains the cheapest way to get real data, and this sweep found nothing that substitutes for it.

Agora's documentation contradicts itself on which events reach a server webhook: the notification event-types page lists 8 types including 104 (token expiry) and 112 (Turns Finished), while the webhooks page lists only 101, 102, 103, 110, 111, 201 and 202. If 112 is client-side only, then turn-level end.type and interrupt_duration_ms are unavailable for pure telephony calls with no client SDK — which would gut the barge-in panel for exactly the deployment that needs it most. This needs a direct answer from the runtime team before the first-24-hours design is specced.

Whether Agora's runtime emits anything privately beyond the documented fields — ASR confidence, alternatives, per-word timing, audio quality/MOS, packet loss — was not established. The docs say no; the code may say otherwise.

Vapi's Simulations scoring is still opaque: the create-simulation body is only scenarioId + personalityId + name + path, and no public endpoint exposes the rubric structure, scorer types or thresholds. The scenario and personality objects themselves would need a separate API-reference pass to spec an import.

No published rollback rate, time-to-detect, or test-before-deploy proportion exists for voice agents specifically. The proxies found here are software-delivery ones (DORA) and vendor marketing (feature-flag ROI claims, which I would not put in a deck). Agora's first quarter still establishes a baseline rather than hitting a number.

The branded-calling and STIR/SHAKEN answer-rate lift figures all trace to vendor blogs (e.g. a claimed 26% pickup lift for one 73-agent team). Hiya's 86% non-answer number is solid; the lift numbers are not, and should not be quoted without a better source.

Did not examine what Agora's own console shows post-call today versus the redesign, so the delta between 'what the runtime emits' and 'what is already rendered in the live Console' is unverified — worth a pass over ng-console's call-detail surfaces before claiming anything is missing from the product rather than from the parser.

northStar.name: Fast Proven Agents (FPA)
northStar.definition: The count of new agents created in a week that (a) reached a verified first answer within 15 minutes of ACTIVE builder time and (b) then held at least one real production conversation of 2 or more turns within 14 days of creation. "Verified first answer" = an agent_test_session whose success is anchored on the runtime's first turn-finished for that agent (server-side), with turnCount >= 1, trigger != 'auto', and configured = true (a voice is set and systemPrompt is non-empty) - so the scripted demo transcript and the 150ms autoTalk auto-start in the prototype cannot qualify. Counted per agent, attributed to the account; the new-account and existing-account series are always reported separately and never summed into one headline.
northStar.formula:
FPA(W) = count of agents A where first operation_succeeded{agent_create} for A falls in ISO week W AND ttfaActiveMs(A) <= 900000 AND there exists a production session for A with turnCount >= 2 starting on or before agent_create(A) + 14 days.
Fast-Proven Rate FPR(W) = FPA(W) / (all agents with a first agent_create in W).
Cohort finalises at W + 14d; the weekly read is therefore the W-2 cohort.
Exclusions (applied identically to numerator and denominator, and both series charted separately per Dmitriev 2017 s5.1): trafficType in {internal, test}; agentSource = 'duplicate'; agt_default and any demo agent; agents whose only test session carries trigger = 'auto'; sessions failing the client/server telemetry-agreement check.
northStar.why: It is the only formulation found that says "fastest to configure and test" AND cannot be gamed by getting faster at nothing. Strip the builder to a Create button that publishes a canned demo and TTFA collapses to 20 seconds - but the agent never holds a real conversation, so FPA falls. It is an outcome (Amplitude: "Never try to influence the North Star directly"), and it is structurally the Netflix-2005 shape the literature names as the closest published analogue to an activation metric: a first-session, time-boxed, threshold-count. The 15-minute threshold is the smallest natural working block a developer ever has (Parnin & Rugaber ICPC 2009, Table 2: 1-3 x 15min, 1-2 x 30min, 1-2 x 1h, 1 x 2h per day) and it beats the most aggressive published end-to-end competitor claim (Retell, "15 minutes", which Retell's own blog restates as "the 30 minute build is the floor"). The "2 or more turns" proof qualifier is the deliberate, honest admission that one successful test call proves the agent can talk, not that it is correct. One threshold (900s) is used three ways - qualification, winsorization, and failure classification - so nobody can compute two different numbers.
northStar.baseline: UNMEASURED and currently UNCOMPUTABLE: there is no test-session event anywhere in ng-console (docs/design/agent-builder-kpis.md s6.1 - "we can see agents being created and published; we cannot see anyone test one"), and the three agent-builder events that do fire (caller_first_selected, ai_disclosure_enabled, greeting_previewed) lose their entire payload to the 48-key camelCase sanitizer allowlist, so even greeting_previewed cannot be tied to an agent. Modelled estimate 4-8 FPA/week, basis: ~1,880 international active customers (last disclosed Agora split, Q2 2025) against total active customers 3,892, +0.4% YoY - implying roughly 30-40 new agents/week company-wide; x an assumed 35-45% verified-test rate (Userpilot 547-company benchmark: mean SaaS activation 37.5%); x an assumed ~50% production-proof rate. Confidence: LOW. This is a placeholder for the W0 two-week baseline and the 20-participant moderated benchmark, not a number to quote.
northStar.target: FPA >= 15/week AND Fast-Proven Rate >= 45%, by the end of the quarter following the W0 baseline close. Both are reported together on purpose: the rate is the half design owns; the count is hostage to new-logo growth, which is running at +0.4% YoY, so a flat count with a rising rate is a design win and must be readable as one. Threshold honesty note, following Amplitude's own admission about the "two other people" in Weekly Learning Users: 45% is aspirational-and-achievable, set at ~1.15x the 37.5% cross-industry SaaS activation mean because zero required credentials should beat the mean, not a derived optimum. Revisit date: 8 weeks after the first clean cohort closes.
northStar.owner: Product owner reports it; Design lead owns the Fast-Proven Rate. A guardrail breach escalates to the named owner of that guardrail (Airbnb's Stat Sig Negative Guardrail escalation idea), which presupposes every row below has one - they do.
northStar.cadence: Weekly, in docs/observability/weekly-report.md as a new "Builder activation" section, always read as the W-2 cohort so the 14-day qualification window has closed. Action threshold (not a target - a trigger): two consecutive weeks with FPR below 30% opens an investigation owned by the Design lead.

guardrails.name: 24-hour rollback / disable rate (DETERIORATION tier - no acceptable margin)
guardrails.definition: Share of successful agent_publish events followed within 24h by any of: agent_deployment_status_update to disabled, a rollback to a prior version, or a re-publish touching the same field group. Numerator and denominator charted as their own series. Population: all publishes, all accounts, weekly.
guardrails.threshold: Point estimate must stay <= 5% at every weekly read. Above it, the newest flagged builder change is reverted before anything else ships - this is a stopping rule, not a hypothesis test. Stated honestly: PostHog's own N = (16 x variance)/d^2 puts detecting a rise from 5% to 7.5% at 1,216 users per arm, which Agora's ~36 first-agents/week will never reach, so this guardrail is a MONITOR. Writing it as "must not rise" without saying that would be theatre.
guardrails.why: Defends FPA against speed-at-any-cost. It is a deterioration metric in Spotify's taxonomy (Schultzberg et al., arXiv 2402.11609) - no bounded regression is acceptable - which is why it gets an inferiority stopping rule rather than a non-inferiority margin. Currently not even observable: there is no version object and no rollback surface in either codebase, so shipping the version/rollback lever (l4.4) is a prerequisite for this guardrail existing at all.

guardrails.name: First-publish failure rate (DETERIORATION tier)
guardrails.definition: operation_failed on the first agent_publish per agent, divided by first agent_publish attempts per agent. Broken down by errorStage. Numerator and denominator on the dashboard as separate series.
guardrails.threshold: <= 5%, checked weekly. Any single weekly read above 8% blocks further builder ships until the errorStage distribution is read.
guardrails.why: A preflight that makes people feel ready and then fails them is worse than no preflight - Buell & Norton (Management Science 57:9, Experiment 5) found that when the outcome is unfavourable, showing the work actively LOWERS perceived value. It is also the metric that tells you whether the preflight checks (l3.1) are aimed at the real failure modes; if failures do not drop, re-derive the checks from errorStage rather than from assumption.

guardrails.name: Evidence-before-live rate (GUARDRAIL tier - non-inferiority, margin -3pp)
guardrails.definition: Share of first publishes preceded by at least one verified voice test session for that agent. Population: first publish per agent, external traffic, weekly.
guardrails.threshold: Non-inferior within -3pp of the prior 4-week mean; absolute floor 85%. If a speed change pushes this below the floor, the change loses even if TTFA wins.
guardrails.why: This is the explicit defence against extremal Goodhart (Manheim & Garrabrant, arXiv 1803.04585): the fastest possible builder is one that deploys without testing, and that variant would win on TTFA and destroy the product. It is the operational form of trade-off assumption A10 - speed vs trust, with trust as the tiebreaker.

guardrails.name: Runtime turn latency per stack (GUARDRAIL tier - non-inferiority, margin +150ms on p95)
guardrails.definition: e2eLatencyMs from the runtime turn-finished payload (already parsed in src/lib/latency-metrics.ts), aggregated p50 and p95 per model stack preset, production sessions only. Reported as OUR measured caller-perceived number; vendor component latency may never be printed as an end-to-end figure.
guardrails.threshold: p50 <= 900ms, p95 <= 1,500ms, and p95 non-inferior within +150ms of the preceding 4-week mean for the same stack. Context: independently measured caller-to-caller medians across the market run 1,296ms (Telnyx) to 1,740ms (Retell), p95 1,768-2,259ms (Openbenchmarks, 108 real phone calls per platform, Silero VAD, Aug 2026). ~1,200ms p50 is where callers begin interrupting (DestiLabs fleet telemetry, 10+ production deployments).
guardrails.why: Guards against winning "fastest to configure" and losing "fastest to answer" - the two clocks share a name and nothing else. Note this also corrects the existing KPI doc s4, which lists Retell at 680ms/920ms next to ElevenLabs 1,424ms and Vapi 1,558ms: that row mixes one server-side figure with two caller-perceived ones and makes Retell look 2x faster than it measures. Fix the table before it reaches the owner.

guardrails.name: Perceived effort at first answer - single-question SEQ (GUARDRAIL tier - non-inferiority, margin -0.3)
guardrails.definition: PostHog Survey, API presentation type so it renders in Studio X components, triggered once per person on agent_test_session succeeded: "How easy was setting up this agent?" 1-7. Plus a second survey on first agent_publish: "How confident are you putting this in front of callers?" 1-5, with free text.
guardrails.threshold: Mean SEQ >= 5.5/7 and non-inferior within -0.3 of the preceding 4-week mean. Confidence >= 3.5/5 on first publish. Free within PostHog's 1,500 survey responses/month tier.
guardrails.why: The single most important counter-metric here, and it is missing from the current doc. Mark, Gudith & Klocke (CHI 2008) found interrupted people complete tasks FASTER with no quality loss but significantly more stress, frustration, time pressure and effort - so a falling TTFA can coexist with a worsening experience and no behavioural metric will show it. Session Replay is disabled by policy, so with HEART's Happiness row having no log-based signal source, the paper's own answer is a survey. Without this, "confidence in production" is entirely behavioural inference with no attitudinal check.

guardrails.name: External share of FPA and agents-per-account (ADVERSARIAL Goodhart guard)
guardrails.definition: FPA split by trafficType (external / internal / test / unclassified) and by whether the creating user is a solutions engineer, plus median and p90 agents created per account per week. Never merged into one number.
guardrails.threshold: External share of FPA >= 70%. Any account creating more than 5 agents in a week is flagged and inspected before its agents count toward FPA.
guardrails.why: Solutions engineers creating agents on customers' behalf inflate the count; so does a demo account. ng-console already auto-classifies any agora.io email as internal (identity.ts DEFAULT_INTERNAL_EMAIL_DOMAINS) - but AuthenticatedObservabilityGate passes no classifyNonProductionAsTest, so preview and local traffic currently falls through to EXTERNAL. Set classifyNonProductionAsTest: true before the redesign goes on a Vercel preview or the baseline is contaminated on day one.

guardrails.name: Telemetry agreement - client vs server test sessions (QUALITY test; the result does not count if this fails)
guardrails.definition: Ratio of client-emitted agent_test_session_succeeded events to server-observed first turn-finished events for the same agent and window. Plus: events by schemaVersion, unclassified-traffic share, and events missing isFirstAgent.
guardrails.threshold: Client/server agreement >= 95%. A gap over 10% between the client-computed ttfaActiveMs and the PostHog funnel's skew-corrected median is a data-quality alarm, not a metric change, and it invalidates that week's read.
guardrails.why: Dmitriev et al. (KDD 2017, s5.3, Telemetry Loss Bias): lost client events are a highly biased set and "practically invalidate any metrics based on the affected events," while server-based metrics stayed valid. A test panel holding a live voice session is exactly where a client drops its last beacon, and ad-blockers silently remove the slow users' start events, biasing TTFA downward. This is Spotify's fourth ship clause - a quality test that must pass before the result counts - and it is the highest-leverage single line in the telemetry plan, because without it the W0 baseline is uninterpretable. Also pre-register Twyman's law here: any variant claiming more than 3 standard deviations of TTFA improvement against the W0 week-to-week variance is investigated for telemetry loss or a changed stop condition before it is read as a win.

tree.name: TTFA - Time To First Answer (active minutes)
tree.definition: Active-time elapsed from operation_started{agent_create} (or import submit) to the verified first answer, with idle gaps over 120s removed and accumulated from visibilitychange deltas, never from a tick counter. ALWAYS written with its unit and never as a bare "TTFA" next to a millisecond number: the voice industry's TTFA means time-to-first-audio with a sub-300ms bar (Hamming/Soniox glossaries), and the runtime clock in this repo is TTFAB (ms). Reported alongside wallMs and resumedCount so "our builder is slow" is separable from "this person had a meeting" - 40% of interrupted tasks are never resumed at all (O'Conaill & Frohlich).
tree.formula: ttfaActiveMs = sum of visible-tab deltas between agent_create and the verified first answer, winsorized at 900,000ms. Report median and p75 when n >= 25; report the geometric mean with a log-transformed CI when n < 25 (Sauro & Lewis CHI 2010: ~13% less error and ~22% less bias than the sample median at small n). Never the arithmetic mean. Successful completions only; sessions exceeding 900s are reported separately as a TTFA-failure rate, not as slow successes. Percentiles come from a Trends percentile aggregation or a SQL insight over the ttfaActiveMs property - NOT from the funnel's time-to-convert view, which exposes median and mean only (PostHog issue #24208, open since Aug 2024).
tree.baseline: Unmeasured. Modelled 8-12 min median on the live console (assumption A0): publish is impossible without free-text system prompt typing (no default system prompt exists anywhere in src/lib/agents), the test call has six preconditions of which the savedPreview check is a SILENT no-op that emits nothing, and the fastest blank path creates a GENERAL_AGENT - the wrong type for the inbound-phone journey. The studio_x_2 prototype's ~0.5s-to-transcript is NOT a baseline: it plays a hard-coded RAIL_TALK script that is not gated on configuration at all. Confidence: low-medium.
tree.target: Median <= 3 min (180s, see budgets), p75 <= 6 min, 900s ceiling. Competitive context: Vapi publishes "under 5 minutes" (9 documented steps, including provisioning a free US number Agora cannot match), LiveKit "less than 10 minutes" but via CLI with a local dev environment, ElevenLabs ~7 dashboard steps, Retell 15 min end-to-end. Every one of those is a scripted-happy-path claim with no definition, population, window, sample size or percentile - so publishing our MEASURED median/p75/p90 with the event definitions attached is itself the differentiator, not the number.
tree.owner: Design lead (builder IA, sections 1-4); Staff front-end engineer owns the instrumentation.

tree.name: VTR - Verified Test Rate
tree.definition: Share of new agents that reach a verified first answer AT ALL within 14 days, regardless of how long it took. Deliberately separate from i1: making testing easier pulls in slower, less confident users, which raises VTR and raises TTFA p75 at the same time. If the two were one metric that trade would be invisible.
tree.formula: VTR(W) = agents in cohort W with >= 1 verified agent_test_session succeeded within 14 days / all agents in cohort W. Server-anchored on the runtime's first turn-finished; the client event is secondary. Breakdown by viewport (>=1024px vs below) as two separate funnels - below 1024px the builder's sticky strip carries step chips and Deploy but NO test door at all, so one TTFA number across both viewports would be a fiction.
tree.baseline: Unmeasured; estimate 35-45%. Basis: Userpilot's 547-company benchmark puts mean SaaS activation at 37.5%; Zuko's 93M-session form benchmark puts software-vertical form completion at 50.6% with credential-type fields the worst offenders at 10.5% mean drop-off. Agora's zero-credential default path should beat both; the silent no-op refusal in the live console probably pulls it below.
tree.target: >= 70% within 14 days, >= 55% in the first session. The 70% is extrapolated, not sourced: it is roughly 1.8x the 37.5% SaaS mean, justified by the default path requiring zero vendor keys, zero payment method and zero keystrokes - if it is not far above the mean, a gate exists that should not.
tree.owner: Design lead; Design researcher validates the refusal taxonomy from moderated sessions.

tree.name: SBDR - Same-Block Deploy Rate (and TTFD)
tree.definition: Share of agents with a verified first answer that go on to a successful publish AND a first production session within 24h, with total active builder time from agent_create under 30 minutes (two 15-minute blocks). TTFD is re-anchored on agent_create, NOT on the TTFA stop, so the two clocks share an origin and are genuinely comparable rather than serial - the previous draft's TTFD started where TTFA stopped, which made any change to the TTFA stop condition mechanically move TTFD.
tree.formula: SBDR(W) = agents with verified test AND operation_succeeded{agent_publish} AND a production session within 24h AND ttfdActiveMs <= 1,800,000 / agents with a verified test. TTFD carries a mandatory blocked_on dimension in {external_carrier, regulatory_review, payment_method, none}; only blocked_on = 'none' counts toward SBDR, and the blocked series is reported beside it. Winsorize TTFD at 24h.
tree.baseline: Unmeasured; estimate 20-30%. Basis: Agora sells and ports NO phone numbers - docs.agora.io requires an active SIP trunk and a SIP-capable number, and the redesign's own sheet says so verbatim ("Bring a number you already own. Agora routes it, and doesn't sell or port numbers"). Independent reviews put Synthflow's real path at 30-60 minutes once telephony is wired. Twilio regulatory bundles take up to 3 business days typically and up to 21 business days in KYC countries - which is why blocked_on is mandatory, not optional.
tree.target: >= 45% with blocked_on = 'none'; TTFD median <= 20 min, p75 <= 45 min of active time. Note the p75 target crosses PostHog's 30-minute idle session boundary, so "same session" must be our own stamped builder_session_id, not $session_id. Segment US vs non-US: outside North America every competitor collapses onto the same bring-your-own-Twilio path Agora requires, so non-US is where SIP Quick-connect is category-leading rather than a consolation.
tree.owner: Design lead (sections 2 and 5); Product owner owns the telephony scope decision.

tree.name: EBL - Evidence Before Live
tree.definition: Share of first publishes that carry a complete evidence ladder: >= 1 verified voice test AND >= 5 scenario runs with a printed verdict AND a preflight evaluated with zero blocking items. The answer to the owner's "how do we build confidence in production" question, expressed as something countable. Independent of i1: you can be fast and evidenced, or slow and unevidenced.
tree.formula: EBL(W) = first publishes meeting all three conditions / all first publishes, weekly, external traffic. Each of the three conditions also charted separately so a fall is attributable. Accompanying quality read: judge-override rate per suite (share of simulated verdicts the builder flipped with "I disagree") - above ~30% the rubric is broken, not the agent.
tree.baseline: Unmeasured; estimate 10-20%. Basis: LangChain's State of Agent Engineering (n=1,340, fielded Nov-Dec 2025) puts 52.4% of teams running offline evals and 37.3% online, with only ~25% of eval-running teams doing both - but that population is agent-framework practitioners, not console users, so read it as a ceiling. Agora ships no simulation surface today and no preflight in the live console, so the floor is near zero for anything but the voice-test leg.
tree.target: >= 60% by end of the quarter after W0, with the voice-test leg alone >= 85% (that leg is also guardrail 3). Extrapolated from the LangChain 52.4% offline-eval figure on the argument that a generated suite should beat what practitioners author by hand.
tree.owner: Design lead (sections 4 and 5); Runtime/voice engineering lead owns the production scorer path.

tree.name: Preset-first model stack with our own measured $/min and p50 printed
tree.definition: Tracker row 03 / assumption A1. The latency-vs-cost slider lands on a named recommended stack with manual config collapsed, and the recap prints Agora's own measured p50 for that stack and the all-in $/min - not vendor component latency, ever. Vapi already ships the identical control (Balanced / High Intelligence / Ultra Fast / Cost Saver) WITH per-preset latency, cost and quality numbers, so the preset itself is table stakes; the measured numbers are the differentiator.
tree.formula: agent_model_stack_selected{mode, preset, costPerMinBucket, ttftBucket} + change-away-from-default rate per control.
tree.baseline: Unmeasured. Every default is already sensible in the prototype (balanced stack 750ms/$0.10/min, all Agora-managed; only name, voice, channels, systemPrompt, greeting, failureMessage are empty on a blank draft, and picking a voice fills three of those).
tree.target: Manual-config rate < 30% of first agents; -30 to -60s median TTFA over 8 weeks, ASSUMING 70% of first agents never open manual config and preset dwell holds at 45s p75. Stated as a Shopify-style range with the assumption falsifiable separately from the effect, and discounted by a 0.33 prior (Microsoft's measured base rate of experiments that move metrics) before it is summed with any other row.

tree.name: Make the draft-testable panel DISCOVERABLE (not possible - it already is)
tree.definition: Assumption A2, rewritten. The capability exists: agent-wizard.tsx carries the header comment "Publish is a HINT, not a gate," toggleTest never checks publish state, and the only thing that disables Talk is the first-run warming flag. So the change cannot buy -60s by making testing possible. The real cost is that the right rail auto-opens on the 'simulations' tab, hiding the Talk button, and nobody knows a draft is testable. Fix: rail defaults to Voice call for a configured agent, and the panel says in copy that it calls the unsaved draft. Retell publishes exactly this guarantee ("free and doesn't need a phone number or payment method... as many times as you want before publishing"); Vapi requires Publish first.
tree.formula: time-to-first-Talk-click from builder mount, p75; agent_test_session_started{agentState, surface: 'rail'|'header'|'opening'|'auto', trigger}. Exclude trigger='auto' from every TTFA read.
tree.baseline: 2 clicks via the header, 1 via "Hear the opening" on the provisioned agent; unmeasured for a cold start.
tree.target: p75 time-to-first-Talk-click <= 40s; share of test sessions on an unsaved draft >= 60%.

tree.name: Endowed progress - the rail opens at "3 of 5 ready", honestly
tree.definition: The defaults really are working values, so render them as progress rather than as an empty checklist. Also fixes a live defect: isDone() hard-codes section 4 as true and section 5 reads a stale isLive computed once at page load, so a blank draft reads "1 of 5" and a just-deployed new agent never reaches 5 of 5 - the only visible progress signal in the page is wrong in both directions.
tree.formula: Instrument blocks_remaining (publishBlocks() already computes it, 9 distinct reasons) as a counter over session time.
tree.baseline: Counter exists and is wrong; no telemetry.
tree.target: -15 to -35% on time from builder mount to first section completion. Extrapolated from Kivetz, Urminsky & Zheng (JMR 2006): a 12-stamp card with 2 stamps pre-filled was completed in a median 10 days vs 15 for an equivalent 10-stamp card - a 33% reduction in time-to-goal from an illusion of progress alone. Ours is not an illusion, which is the whole argument for shipping it.

tree.name: Extend seed-from-voice; close the two hard page-exits
tree.definition: Picking a voice already fills name, systemPrompt and greeting (seedFromVoice), satisfying two of the four publish blocks in one click - protect and extend it to seed the channel. Separately, close the two exits on a REQUIRED path: Create credential does a full window.location.assign('/project/vendor-credentials') from inside a sheet inside an expander (React state destroyed, no return path), and Add Connector is a router.push with no inline alternative. Nine other exits are optional hint links.
tree.formula: builder_exit{target, section, required: boolean}; credential_page_exit{slot, vendor, agentId} fired BEFORE the assign.
tree.baseline: 7 clicks / 0 keystrokes / 0 API keys from blank draft to a deployed inbound agent (vs 4 clicks in the live console, but those 4 require mandatory free-text prompt writing). Frame the claim as "zero keystrokes and zero credential decisions", never as fewer clicks - on raw clicks the redesign looks slower.
tree.target: Required-path exits per first agent = 0. 7 clicks -> 5.

tree.name: One duration-aware loading-state machine for the whole builder
tree.definition: Per NN/g's actual rule (not the 400ms-3s band that circulates secondhand): under ~1s show nothing; 2-10s a spinner scoped to the module or a skeleton for a full-page load; over 10s a determinate progress bar with named work and a cancel. A skeleton on a fast page is actively annoying. Narrated operational transparency is licensed ONLY for genuinely slow, reliable steps (knowledge-base ingestion, SIP provisioning) - never for a voice preview or model switch, whose expectation anchor is sub-second, and NEVER paired with a step that can fail: Buell & Norton's Experiment 5 found transparency lowers perceived value when the outcome is bad, and their decline point was 30s in one context and 15s in another depending on what users expect the service to take.
tree.formula: interaction_latency_ms on slider drag, sheet open, voice preview, model switch; alarm above 400ms p90 (Doherty). Quote the 400ms threshold externally but NOT the 25-30% productivity figure - the canonical Doherty & Thadani mirror is dead and the claim is unverifiable.
tree.baseline: SipQuickConnect already does this correctly with a timestamped fact-log instead of a spinner; the deploy preflight adds 1,090ms of pure cosmetic settle time; the test panel's warming state is a disabled button with no explanation.
tree.target: Every non-network control under 400ms p90; no blocking step over 10s without named work and a cancel.

tree.name: A test door below 1024px
tree.definition: The builder header is a single non-wrapping 64px flex row with five shrink-0 controls and no wrap or overflow rules; the lg:hidden mobile strip that replaces it carries step chips and Deploy but no Voice call control at all, and the test panel's Sheet fallback is never auto-opened. On a phone the 2-click TTFA does not exist - the only route is "Hear the opening" inside section 3, after a ~5,000px scroll.
tree.formula: VTR and TTFA reported as two separate funnels split at 1024px. Never quote one number across both.
tree.baseline: Below 1024px: no test door. AUDIT.md line 241 already records "mobile layouts break at the header".
tree.target: VTR below 1024px within 10pp of desktop.

tree.name: Instrument every refusal, starting with the silent ones
tree.definition: ng-console's handleStartPreview has six early returns and the first - no savedPreview - is a silent no-op: no error, no state change, no telemetry. It is the single largest TTFA failure in the product and it is invisible. Every early return gets an operation_failed-shaped event with a reason. Same treatment for the 9 publishBlocks reasons, fired as deploy_blocked{reason, step} on every deploy click.
tree.formula: test_refused{reason} and deploy_blocked{reason, step}; the blocked-reason taxonomy is closed and small (9 publish reasons, 6 test preconditions).
tree.baseline: Zero refusal telemetry in either codebase. Three track() call sites exist in the entire prototype builder, one of which reports a hard-coded duration_sec: 30 with no timer.
tree.target: 100% of refusals emit a reason; the top refusal reason named within one week of W0.

tree.name: Surface and measure the microphone permission step
tree.definition: usePreviewAudioDevices calls navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia on the real preview path. That is an OS prompt no click count captures, it can add seconds, and it can fail outright - an unbounded unmeasured step sitting inside the TTFA clock. Pre-explain it, then instrument grant/deny/timeout.
tree.formula: mic_permission{result: 'granted'|'denied'|'dismissed', durationMs}.
tree.baseline: Unmeasured and unexplained.
tree.target: Grant rate >= 90%; permission step <= 12s p75 (it owns 12 of the 25s connect budget).

tree.name: Logged-out "hear an Agora agent"
tree.definition: Bland puts "Click to speak with an agent" in front of anonymous visitors across four verticals; LiveKit's Agent Builder previews in-browser with zero local setup. Every part already exists in the prototype - the TalkTab, a default managed stack, a default voice - so this is a routing and quota problem, not a build. It is the only TTFA measurement that can ever reach zero minutes, and it gives PostHog an anonymous-to-identified join point. Note anonymous events are up to 4x cheaper than identified ones, and ng-console currently identifies before first render so 100% of its events are identified.
tree.formula: agent_test_started{authState: 'anonymous'}; signup conversion read from the anonymous cohort.
tree.baseline: Does not exist; Agora's shipped ConvoAI Playground sits behind a login and still asks for an LLM API Key.
tree.target: Own tracker row and own assumption; no effect claimed until measured.

tree.name: Preflight that lists every blocker at once, and never closes itself
tree.definition: Tracker row 05 / assumption A8. The live console's validateAgentDetailDraft is a chain of early returns that can never return more than one issue, and handleDetailPublishConfirm re-runs the check inside the dialog and CLOSES it on failure - so N blockers cost N publish attempts and the dialog vanishes mid-action. Listing all blockers collapses N attempts to 1. Two-tier it the way Google SRE two-tiered launch reviews (30% of launches got the abbreviated checklist): a first inbound web-widget deploy on managed keys gets three items; an outbound batch campaign on a new BYO credential gets the full list. And print what was NOT checked as plainly as what passed - an all-green screen that silently omits "nobody has tested the refund path" manufactures the false confidence the checklist exists to prevent.
tree.formula: agent_preflight_evaluated{blockingCount, warningCount, tier}; preflight_opened / _fix_clicked{rowId} / _talk_first / _abandoned / _confirmed. All five are currently unfired.
tree.baseline: Live console: 1 blocker per attempt, dialog self-closes. Prototype: preflight exists, fully untracked, 1,090ms of cosmetic settle.
tree.target: First-publish failure -50%; deploy dwell cost +15s or less. Governance rule adopted from Google SRE: no preflight item ships without a named failure it would have caught.

tree.name: SIP Quick-connect as the default phone path, region-segmented
tree.definition: Quick-connect takes one pasted Twilio/Telnyx credential and auto-enumerates, auto-picks and auto-attaches a number in <= 4 inputs; the manual form demands 6 required fields plus a transport choice. Sell the import, never the provisioning - Agora does not sell or port numbers, which is a US-only deficit: outside North America Vapi (US-only free number, inbound-only), Retell (US/CA only), LiveKit (US-only, inbound-only) and ElevenLabs (never sold numbers) all collapse onto the same bring-your-own-Twilio path.
tree.formula: TTFD segmented US / non-US with blocked_on; quick-connect vs manual attach rate.
tree.baseline: Quick-connect is already fully instrumented in the prototype - the only path that is.
tree.target: Quick-connect chosen for >= 70% of phone attachments; non-US TTFD published as its own column.

tree.name: Reorder the rail so the happy path is Prompt -> Test
tree.definition: STEP_TITLES is Voice & Models -> Deployment -> Prompt & knowledge -> Test -> Go Live, so a channel decision (a radio, not multi-select) sits upstream of first sound. Every competitor that wins on TTFA defers channel entirely and puts prompt-then-test first; Retell explicitly places every commercial and credential gate downstream of the free browser test. Either move Deployment after Test, or keep the order and ship sections 1 and 2 fully collapsed with defaults applied.
tree.formula: section_index_at_first_test - if the median is above 1, the IA is still pushing people through configuration first.
tree.baseline: Test is 4th of 5.
tree.target: median section_index_at_first_test = 1.

tree.name: Stay in the builder after deploy
tree.definition: publishDeployment ends with router.push('/monitor') for every channel except code, and clears the draft. The funnel's last step is an exit, and the moment where confidence has to be built happens on a different page with no agent context beyond query params. Keep the user in place with a live-status panel, or make /monitor?deployed= a real first-call watch.
tree.formula: Gap between deployment_went_live and first_real_call_received - the true "is it working in production?" metric, and the input to MTTD.
tree.baseline: Exit on every deploy; no first-call event exists.
tree.target: First-call watch opened on >= 70% of first deploys.

tree.name: Generated scenario suite - never a blank authoring state
tree.definition: Assumption A9. Generate ~20 starter scenarios from the agent's own prompt, tools and Opening config the moment section 3 completes, in the published 40% happy-path / 30% edge / 15% error / 10% adversarial / 5% acoustic mix, with a 50 / 200 / 500 ladder shown as honest progress ("12 of 50 minimum scenarios"). Label each run pass^k ("5 of 5 runs passed"), not pass. Surface a saturation nudge at 100% - a suite everything passes carries no signal (Anthropic; Hamel Husain puts an informative pass rate near 70%). Fix the default that guarantees a red row: DEFAULT_CALL_BEHAVIOR.transfer = false makes the "asks for a human" scenario always fail.
tree.formula: agent_simulation_run{scenarioCount, passCount, judge: 'llm'|'rule', mix}; suite growth from production failures per agent per week.
tree.baseline: No simulation surface ships. Binary verdicts with named assertion kinds already exist in eval-tests.tsx - defend that against any request for a 0-100 quality score (Likert adjacent points are subjectively inconsistent across annotators).
tree.target: >= 5 scenario runs before first publish on >= 60% of agents.

tree.name: One rubric, offline and online
tree.definition: At Go Live, offer the assertions authored in section 4 as the PRODUCTION success criteria - one checkbox, "Keep scoring live calls against these 12 checks." ElevenLabs is the only competitor that evaluates simulations with the same criteria applied in production; Vapi does the production half separately via Scorecards. Only ~25% of eval-running teams do both offline and online, which is exactly where confidence leaks. This makes "agents with an eval suite" and "live agents with production scorers" the same number, with zero new authoring.
tree.formula: Share of live agents with production scorers attached; agreement between offline verdict and online score per agent.
tree.baseline: Neither half exists.
tree.target: >= 50% of first deploys keep the rubric live.

tree.name: Rule-of-three canary with the bound printed
tree.definition: "Watch the next N calls" - count-based, not percentage-based, because a 10% split on an agent taking 30 calls a day yields 3 calls and canary comparisons need ~50 data points per metric to mean anything. Print the maths in the UI: zero failures in n trials bounds the true failure rate at 3/n with 95% confidence, so 20 clean calls still allows 15%, 60 allows 5%, 100 allows 3%, 300 allows 1% (Hanley & Lippman-Hand, JAMA 1983). Set the auto-rollback condition AT deploy time, in the user's own words. Nobody in the category shows this, and it is honest rather than reassuring - which is what calibrated trust requires (Lee & See 2004: the goal is calibrated trust, not maximum trust).
tree.formula: canary_started{n, rollbackRule} / canary_completed{failures, boundPct}; MTTD = time from a bad publish to the builder knowing.
tree.baseline: No canary, no rollback rule, no MTTD. Users currently discover bad deploys via tickets.
tree.target: Canary used on >= 40% of first deploys; MTTD median <= 30 min. MTTD is the metric a console can uniquely drive to minutes and no voice competitor advertises.

tree.name: Immutable versions, one-click rollback, and an honest rollback scope
tree.definition: Retell shipped versioning with percentage traffic splitting in 2026; ElevenLabs ships branch-based versioning with deterministic routing - but documents no rollback procedure at all. Synthflow ships one-click revert that silently excludes actions and knowledge bases. So: ship immutable published versions with the number on the deploy bar, an actual one-click rollback, and a confirmation that NAMES what is restored and what is not (MCP servers, connectors, knowledge base). Two lines of UI that convert a trust trap into a trust builder. config_drift_detected already carries ran_version and current_version, so a version concept is half-present in the front end - name it.
tree.formula: version_promoted{versionId}; rollback_performed{versionId, reason, scopeExcluded[]}.
tree.baseline: No version object, no rollback surface. The header CTA 'Live. No changes' is a no-op primary that only toasts - it records deploy intent with no outcome and must become a status chip or fire deploy_noop.
tree.target: Rollback available on 100% of deploys; guardrail 1 becomes observable.

tree.name: First-24-hours review panel
tree.definition: Answer rate first, above every latency number - 86% of consumers do not answer calls from unknown numbers (Hiya, Censuswide n>12,000), so an agent showing 95% success on 6 answered calls out of 100 dialled is not a working deployment. Then a four-step call funnel (dialled -> ringing -> answered -> completed), computable today from Agora events 201/202 which already carry START/CALLING/RINGING/ANSWERED/HANGUP with report_ms. Then abandonment against the 2-3% / 5-6% / >10% bands with the leading indicators ranked. Then end reasons grouped BY WHO CAN FIX IT - caller behaviour / your configuration (deep-linked to the section) / Agora infrastructure / vendor credential - a grouping the managed-key default makes possible, since a whole class of 401/429/quota reasons does not exist for default agents. Drop ASR confidence from the spec: Agora emits none anywhere.
tree.formula: Console-owned end-reason enum derived from event 102 status/message x event 110 module+code x event 201/202 terminal state. Extend LatencyTurn with startType, endType and interruptDurationMs - parseTurnFinishedMessage currently discards all three, which is why missed-interruption rate and silence-timeout rate are one parser change away, not a backend project.
tree.baseline: Agora has no end-reason taxonomy (status STOPPED|FAILED plus free text) where Vapi publishes 50+ values and Retell ~30, each with a per-reason fix.
tree.target: First-24-hours panel opened on >= 70% of first deploys; every end reason mapped to an owner and a fix.

funnel.definition: From the first paint of the builder route to the moment the user commits to building something: operation_started{agent_create}, a template pick, an import submit, or the first update(patch) on a blank draft. Every draft write already funnels through one update() callback in agent-wizard.tsx, so one throttled hook there yields per-field engagement across twelve components without touching any of them - throttled to once per field per session, because ng-console identifies before first render and 100% of its events are billed as identified.
funnel.startEvent: page_viewed{routePattern: '/agents/:id/edit', isFirstAgent: true} - note ng-console currently sets capture_pageview: false with no manual replacement, and capture_pageleave defaults to 'if_capture_pageview', so BOTH halves of the dwell pair are missing today.
funnel.targetDuration: <= 30s (budget stages 1-2: 15s orient + 20s intent, with 5s of slack)
funnel.dropRisk: The first 10 seconds decide whether anyone stays (NN/g, 205,873 pages, 2bn dwell times); the leave-rate flattens after ~30s. The first paint must make three things legible in that window: an agent already exists and is configured, no API keys are needed, and where the test button is. Working against it: the rail auto-opens on the 'simulations' tab, hiding the Talk button; one click on the rail close button writes a localStorage flag that permanently changes the shortest path for that browser, on every agent, forever - so any TTFA expressed as a click count is wrong for returning users, and rail state must ride along as a property.

funnel.definition: The headline clock. Ends at the first VERIFIED answer: a test session whose success is anchored on the runtime's first turn-finished for that agent, turnCount >= 1, trigger != 'auto', configured = true. The client event is secondary and is cross-checked against the server count weekly (guardrail 7). Refinement path committed now, not later, so v2 and v3 are a redefinition rather than a re-instrumentation - log turnCount and e2eLatencyBucket from day one: v1 = turnCount >= 1; v2 = turnCount >= 3 (they actually had a conversation); v3 = turnCount >= 3 AND an acceptable e2eLatencyBucket (they heard a GOOD agent). This is Amazon's detail-pages -> detail-page-views -> in-stock -> Fast Track In Stock path, written down in advance.
funnel.targetDuration: median <= 3 min (180s), p75 <= 6 min, 900s ceiling above which the session is a failure, not a slow success
funnel.targetConversion: >= 70% within 14 days; >= 55% in the first session
funnel.dropRisk: The microphone permission prompt - unbounded, unmeasured, can fail outright. The warming flag, now the only thing standing between mount and first audio, currently rendered as a dead disabled button. Credential creation doing a full window.location.assign out of a sheet inside an expander, destroying React state with no return path. On the measurement side: the prototype's Talk surface is not gated by configuration at all and plays a hard-coded five-turn script, so a naive TTFA would count canned-demo plays as agent tests; and agent_test_ended fires only from the toggle, with no unmount cleanup and a hard-coded duration_sec: 30, so closing the rail leaves the session open forever. Copy the live console's idiom - a useEffect cleanup keyed on agent id, with a real elapsed time and reason in {toggle, rail_closed, unmount, navigated}.

funnel.definition: From the verified first answer to a scenario suite run with a printed verdict: >= 5 scenarios, each labelled with what it actually exercised. A green suite that never made a sound is the most dangerous confidence signal the builder could show - LiveKit's own test harness explicitly makes no room connection, so ASR, endpointing, barge-in and TTS go untested; and practitioners estimate ~25% of caller-impacting failures are invisible in a transcript. Every saved case carries a fidelity badge: transcript replay vs audio replay.
funnel.endEvent: operation_succeeded{agent_simulation_run} with scenarioCount >= 5 and a verdict rendered
funnel.targetDuration: <= 4 min active (suite generation is 900ms, a full run 1,200ms in the prototype; the time is reading and judging, not machine time)
funnel.dropRisk: A blank authoring state - only 52.4% of teams run offline evals at all, and that figure is from agent-framework practitioners. The suite must be generated from the agent's own prompt, tools and Opening config, never created from scratch. Second risk: the LLM judge. It agrees with humans ~70% of the time and carries position, verbosity and self-preference bias, so every failing verdict must show its evidence anchored to the offending turn (flaggedTurnIndex already does this - keep it) and offer a one-click "I disagree" that flips the verdict and logs it. The Go Live gate says "no test disagreed", never "the agent is safe". Third: the transfer = false default guarantees the "asks for a human" scenario fails on every inbound agent.

funnel.definition: From the scenario verdict to a successful publish AND a first production session within 24h - a publish nobody calls is not a deploy. TTFD is measured from agent_create (shared origin with TTFA, so the two are comparable rather than serial) and carries a mandatory blocked_on dimension so a 3-day carrier wait never contaminates the builder's own clock. The Deployment section needs a suspend/resume state so a user parked on carrier approval is not scored as abandonment.
funnel.startEvent: operation_succeeded{agent_simulation_run} (step conversion); clock anchored at agent_create
funnel.endEvent: operation_succeeded{agent_publish} AND first production session within 24h
funnel.targetDuration: <= 5 min active from the verdict; TTFD median <= 20 min, p75 <= 45 min, blocked_on = 'none' only
funnel.targetConversion: >= 75% (blocked_on = 'none'); report the carrier-blocked cohort separately, never as a loss
funnel.dropRisk: Agora sells and ports no phone numbers, so the phone path requires a SIP trunk the user already owns (6 required fields manually, <= 4 via Quick-connect) - and outside the US every competitor has the same problem, which is where Quick-connect becomes a lead rather than a gap. Twilio regulatory bundles run up to 3 business days typically and up to 21 in KYC countries, and a Twilio trial project cannot provision more than one number or call unverified caller IDs. Inside the product: blockers revealed one at a time in the live console (N blockers = N attempts, dialog self-closing on failure), the 'Live. No changes' no-op primary that records deploy intent with no outcome, and the forced router.push to /monitor that makes the funnel's last step an exit.

funnel.definition: The agent holds at least one real production conversation of >= 2 turns, survives 24h with no rollback or disable, and the builder actually looks at the first-24-hours review. Confidence is a layered ladder, not one test - Anthropic's Swiss-cheese framing: automated evals pre-launch, production monitoring as ground truth, transcript review to recalibrate the judge. The Go Live screen prints the ladder with the holes visible: "Tested by you: 1 voice call - Simulated: 12/12 scenarios - Real callers: 0 - Human-reviewed transcripts: 0", plus a generated "known weak spots" block. Design this screen for a sceptic: DORA 2025 found 90% AI adoption against only 24% of practitioners trusting AI a great deal, with 30% trusting it a little or not at all. Copy that asserts readiness will read as marketing; show evidence and let the user conclude.
funnel.endEvent: first production session with turnCount >= 2 AND no rollback/disable/hotfix-republish within 24h AND first-24-hours review opened
funnel.targetDuration: first real call <= 60 min for a web widget; the trust window itself is 24h; MTTD (bad publish -> builder knows) median <= 30 min
funnel.dropRisk: For outbound, the dominant failure has nothing to do with the prompt: 86% of consumers do not answer unknown numbers, so caller-ID presentation and attestation decide whether the agent ever speaks - answer rate belongs above every latency number on this panel. For inbound, the risk is that nothing calls at all and the builder never learns. And the deepest risk is measurement: 20 clean calls bound the true failure rate at only 15% (rule of three), so a screen of green ticks after a handful of calls manufactures exactly the over-trust that Lee & See's calibration model warns about. Print the bound.

budgets.stage: 1. Orient - first paint to first meaningful interaction
budgets.note: NN/g's dwell analysis of 205,873 pages: the first 10 seconds of a page visit are critical and the leave-rate only flattens after ~30s. Three seconds of this is our own first paint (Google: 53% of mobile visits are abandoned above 3s); the remaining 12 is the human reading the screen and deciding it is worth continuing. Everything they need in that window - an agent already exists, no keys are needed, here is the test button - must be above the fold, which is why the docked test panel being visible on load is doing real work and must not be collapsed by default.

budgets.stage: 2. Declare intent - create dialog, template pick, or import
budgets.note: One required field ("What do you want to build?") or a template card. Typing one sentence is ~12-15s; a template or import is ~5s. Vapi's equivalent is two required text decisions and Retell's is a template pick, so this is parity, not advantage. Import is the fast lane: Postman measured a first successful API call at 17 min unaided and 10 min with a provided collection (1.7x), which is the honest order of effect to expect from import and templates - not an order of magnitude.

budgets.stage: 3. Voice and stack - accept the default stack, pick a recommended voice
budgets.note: Zero required decisions on the stack: the balanced preset (750ms, $0.10/min, all Agora-managed) is already applied, and picking a voice also fills name, system prompt and greeting via seedFromVoice. So the 50s is voice audition only: ~3 previews at ~8s each (assumption A5 takes previews from 6 to 3 by ranking with a printed reason) plus ~26s to scan and commit. The section's p75 budget stays 45s preset + 90s voice = 135s; this is the median path, which A11 assumes the defaults carry. Do not spend design effort pruning the voice catalogue - Hick's law does not apply to scanning a named list and the choice-overload effect is ~zero across 63 conditions and 50 experiments (Scheibehenne et al., JCR 2010). Search and a pre-selected recommendation fix scanning time; hiding options would not.

budgets.stage: 4. Opening and prompt - edit the seeded greeting
budgets.note: seedFromVoice has already written a working prompt and greeting, so the median user edits one line rather than composing from blank. The existing s2.3 p75 budget of 5 minutes is the writer's path, not the median one, and both should be reported. The design principle is fewer REQUIRED decisions, not fewer fields - multi-step forms beat single-step even with more questions (BrokerNotes +35%, Vendio +59%), while field-removal tests now mostly land under 5% lift and one Unbounce client lost 14% by cutting fields. Keep required_decisions_made before first test at <= 3.

budgets.stage: 5. Reach the test - open the panel and press Talk
budgets.note: One click via "Hear the opening" in section 3 (which calls openTest and toggleTest together) or two via the header. Machine time here is a Doherty problem, not a budget problem - every control under 400ms. The 10s is scan-and-decide, and it is the stage assumption A2 is really about: the draft is ALREADY testable with no publish gate ("Publish is a HINT, not a gate" is a comment in the shipped wizard), so the cost is discoverability, not capability. Vapi by contrast requires Publish then Quick Publish before Talk.

budgets.stage: 6. Connect - mic permission, session join, first-run warm-up
budgets.note: Budgeted 12s human (the OS permission prompt, currently unbounded and unmeasured) + 8s join + 5s warm-up. This is the only stage that can plausibly blow past Nielsen's 10-second attention limit, so it is the one stage that earns a determinate progress state with named work and a cancel. But keep the narration short and generic: the expectation anchor for "make my agent talk" is ChatGPT voice mode, so the labour-illusion window here is nearer 15 seconds than 30 (Buell & Norton s4.1), and a rich narration followed by a failed test call is measurably WORSE than a bare spinner followed by the same failure. Never narrate a step that can fail.

budgets.stage: 7. First agent audio - greeting playback begins
budgets.note: First-turn setup plus the opening line starting. The runtime clock inside this stage is TTFAB (milliseconds), target p50 <= 900ms / p95 <= 1,500ms per stack, against independently measured caller-perceived medians of 1,296ms (Telnyx) to 1,740ms (Retell) over 108 real calls per platform. The prototype's SimTranscript reveals turn 1 at 500ms and runs 1,200ms per turn thereafter - that is a scripted number and must not be quoted as a measurement. TOTAL: 15 + 20 + 50 + 45 + 10 + 25 + 15 = 180s = the 3-minute median TTFA target. The p75 target of 6 min is this budget with the voice, prompt and connect stages at their own p75s; the 900s ceiling is not a sum at all - it is the smallest natural working block a developer has (Parnin & Rugaber, Table 2) and it deliberately replaces the earlier 600s ceiling, which was only an arithmetic sum of p75 dwell budgets with no external grounding.

tree.definitionsNote: Every metric here carries eight fields so two people compute the same number: name, one-sentence definition, formula with numerator AND denominator named, population, window, exclusions, owner, cadence - plus target and guardrail. The exclusions line is the one the current doc is missing everywhere, so it is fixed once, globally: excluded from every metric are trafficType in {internal, test} (kept visible as its own series, never globally filtered out), agentSource='duplicate', agt_default and demo agents, test sessions with trigger='auto' (the prototype fires agent_test_started 150ms after mount with no user action), and resumed sessions counted once per agent rather than per sitting. GSM chain, stated explicitly because HEART's whole contribution is the middle step: GOAL = a builder reaches a working, trusted agent inside one short working block. SIGNALS that it went well = a verified answer heard, scenarios run with a verdict, a publish that survives 24h, a real caller served. SIGNALS that it went badly (failure is easier to detect than success) = agent_config_reverted, sheet_abandoned_without_save, test_refused{reason}, deploy_blocked{reason}, credential_page_exit, draft_resumed{ageMs}. METRICS are only ever derived from those signals. HEART scope is declared: Task Success and Adoption carry this product, Retention is the 14-day proof qualifier, Happiness is the SEQ survey, and Engagement is deliberately OUT - more time in the builder is bad, so nobody may add an engagement metric later. Measurement rules that bind every number: durations come from an explicit numeric duration property on the completion event read through a Trends percentile aggregation or SQL quantile(), never from PostHog's funnel time-to-convert view, which exposes median and mean only; report median/p75 at n>=25 and the geometric mean with a log-CI below it; winsorize TTFA at 900s and TTFD at 24h; never the arithmetic mean. Funnel conversion windows are pinned explicitly (TTFA 1 hour for the same-sitting read, 14 days for the eventual read) because PostHog's default is 14 days, and Sequential order is pinned because autocapture makes strict order unusable. Finally, the volume reality that governs all of it: with roughly 1,880 international accounts and total customers growing 0.4% YoY, the builder sees tens of first agents per week, not thousands - PostHog will not even render an experiment estimate below 100 exposures per variant, the rollback guardrail would need 1,216 per arm and tested-before-live 816. So feature flags here are for staged rollout and kill switches, not causal inference; guardrails are monitors with stopping rules, not powered tests; the primary evidence for any TTFA claim is a pre-declared before/after against the W0 two-week baseline plus a 20-participant moderated benchmark timed exactly as TTFA is defined (n=20 gives under 20% margin of error on task time at 95% confidence), reported as a geometric mean with a log-CI. CUPED cannot rescue this: first-agent builders have no pre-experiment period by definition.

conventions: NAMING — freeze `snake_case`, `object_verb`, PAST TENSE (`agent_test_started`, `deploy_blocked`). PostHog's own docs contradict themselves (best-practices page says present tense `category:object_action`; JS SDK page says past tense `object verb`), so this is an Agora decision, not a PostHog one. studio_x_2/lib/analytics.ts already declares this rule at the top of the file and has 88 `track()` call sites obeying it — do not churn them. Allowed verbs: opened, closed, started, ended, completed, selected, changed, configured, previewed, edited, generated, clicked, blocked, succeeded, failed, received, reviewed, promoted, rolled_back, exited, resumed, rated, imported, linked.

PROPERTY CASING — camelCase, wire-compatible with ng-console. ng-console/src/lib/observability/sanitize.ts silently DROPS any property not on a 48-key camelCase allowlist (`durationMs`, `routePattern`, `productArea`, `trigger`, `scenario`, `surface`, `operation`, `result`, `errorStage`…). studio_x_2's stub emits snake_case (`agent_id`, `time_to_live_ms`), which would arrive in PostHog as events with NO properties. Decision: studio_x_2 converts to camelCase (it has zero production data); ng-console extends the allowlist with the builder keys below. Do this in ONE PR before any new event ships, or the funnel will look instrumented and be un-sliceable.

ALLOWLIST ADDITIONS required in ng-console/src/lib/observability/sanitize.ts before wave 0: agentId, agentState, builderSessionId, section, sectionIndex, isFirstAgent, channel, preset, pipeline, vendor, slot, credentialMode, voiceId, voiceVendor, blockedReason, blockedStep, blockCount, warnCount, wallMs, activeMs, resumeCount, turnCount, e2eLatencyBucket, verdict, passCount, failCount, scenarioCount, configured, heardOwnGreeting, railOpen, viewport, versionId, canaryCalls, endReason. This one change also retroactively fixes three already-firing live events — `caller_first_selected`, `ai_disclosure_enabled`, `greeting_previewed` in ng-console/src/components/console/agent-opening-section.tsx (lines 114/129/186) currently lose `agentId` and `seconds` entirely.

BASE PROPERTIES go on `posthog.register()` at init/identify, never per-call: schemaVersion, release, environment, eventSource, productArea='agent_builder', isInternalUser, isTestUser, trafficType, cid, accountUid, isFirstAgent. Enforce the allowlist in posthog-js `before_send`, not only in the facade — sanitize.ts today proves intent, `before_send` proves behaviour. Note posthog-js may be imported ONLY from ng-console/src/lib/observability/posthog-client.ts (enforced by src/lib/observability/sdk-import-guard.ts) — so studio_x_2's `track()` must become a thin facade call, not its own PostHog client.

RENAME THE CLOCK. 'TTFA' is already an industry term meaning Time To First Audio, measured in milliseconds (Hamming's pre-launch gate is TTFA < 800 ms). Using it for a minutes-scale onboarding metric guarantees permanent confusion in every review with a voice engineer. Call the onboarding clock **TTFT — Time To First Talk**; keep TTFA for the runtime per-turn metric. Five-minute fix now, unfixable once it is a dashboard title.

TTFT DEFINITION (the headline speed metric). Start = `builder_opened` where `isFirstAgent=true`, keyed on `builderSessionId`. Stop = `agent_audio_heard` with `trigger != 'auto'` AND `configured=true` AND `turnCount >= 1`. Reported as THREE numbers on the stop event: `wallMs` (persisted Date.now delta across reloads), `activeMs` (visibility-aware accumulation — the primary design metric), `resumeCount` (separate sittings). Winsorize at 600 000 ms; sessions past the ceiling are counted as a separate failure rate, never as long successes. Report median + p75 when n>=25, geometric mean with log-transformed CI when n<25 (Sauro & Lewis). NEVER report the arithmetic mean. Population: first agents only; exclusions declared per metric-definitions.md.

TTFT REFINEMENT PATH, committed now so v2/v3 are a redefinition not a re-instrumentation: v1 = first audio heard with turnCount>=1; v2 = turnCount>=3 (they had a conversation); v3 = turnCount>=3 AND e2eLatencyBucket acceptable (they heard a GOOD agent). Log `turnCount` and `e2eLatencyBucket` on `agent_audio_heard` from day one so all three are computable retroactively (Amazon's detail-page→detail-page-view→in-stock→Fast-Track refinement pattern).

TTFD DEFINITION (time to deployed agent). Start = the SAME `builder_opened` origin as TTFT, not `agent_audio_heard` — re-anchoring both clocks on one origin is what makes them comparable and stops TTFD moving mechanically whenever the TTFT stop condition is edited. Stop = `deployment_went_live`. Emit `wallMs`, `activeMs`, `resumeCount`, plus `blockedOn` ∈ none | external_carrier | regulatory_review | payment_method | credential — a Twilio regulatory bundle takes up to 3 business days (21 in KYC countries) and must not contaminate the builder's own clock. Winsorize at 24 h. Report `activeMs` as the design metric and `wallMs` as the honest customer-experience number, side by side.

CURRENT DURATION CODE IS BROKEN AND MUST BE REPLACED FIRST. studio_x_2/lib/analytics.ts: `timeToLiveMs()` calls `localStorage.removeItem()` BEFORE returning, so a failed dispatch or a React StrictMode double-invoke destroys the measurement with no retry; `markBuildStart()` writes only `if (!localStorage.getItem(...))` so a returning user's second agent is still measured from their first-ever builder mount (a four-day 'time to live'); `agent_test_ended` sends `duration_sec: 30` as a LITERAL with no timer; `time_to_live_ms` is a measurement used as an event name; and `duration_sec` vs ng-console's `durationMs` is two units for one clock. Replace all of it with one `useDurationClock(scopeKey)` hook: stamp per `agentId + builderSessionId`, expire after 2 h idle, clear only in the capture callback, milliseconds everywhere.

CLOCK MECHANICS. `performance.now()` deltas for within-page active time (monotonic, immune to NTP/system-clock jumps); a persisted `Date.now()` stamp only for spans that cross a reload. Never mix them. Accumulate `activeMs` from `visibilitychange` + Date.now deltas, never from a `setInterval`/rAF tick counter — background tabs throttle those to >=1 s or freeze them entirely. Never write a duration to a person property with `$set` (PostHog sets person properties in INGESTION order, not timestamp order, so a late event overwrites it); use `$set_once` for first-time milestones only.

SERVER ANCHOR FOR THE STOP EVENT. `agent_audio_heard` fired purely client-side is exposed to telemetry-loss bias — the exact failure that invalidated every client-event metric in Microsoft's mobile experiment — and a live voice session is precisely where a client drops its last beacon. Anchor the canonical stop on the runtime's first turn-finished for that agent (ng-console/src/lib/latency-metrics.ts already parses Agora notification event 112) and keep the client event as secondary. Ship a data-quality insight comparing client `agent_audio_heard` count to server turn count from day one; without it the wave-0 baseline is uninterpretable.

MEASURE PER PERSON OVER A WINDOW, NOT PER SESSION. A PostHog session ends after 30 min idle or 24 h total, and TTFD's p75 target routinely crosses that boundary; 40% of interrupted tasks are never resumed in the same sitting at all. Build TWO funnels per clock, never one: 'same sitting' with a 60-minute conversion window (the number quoted against the target) and 'eventual' with a 7-day window (the number that feeds activation). The gap between them IS the multi-session finding.

FUNNEL ORDER = Sequential, pinned in the spec with a comment. ng-console runs `autocapture: true`, so Strict order (no events in between) would report near-zero conversion on every builder funnel. Mark every KPI event Verified in Data Management so funnels are never assembled from an autocapture lookalike.

THE FUNNEL'S PERCENTILES CANNOT COME FROM THE FUNNEL. PostHog's time-to-convert view exposes median and mean only — no p75/p90 (open issue #24208). Every p75 in the KPI doc must come from a numeric duration property read through a Trends percentile aggregation (75th/90th/95th/99th are the only options) or a HogQL `quantile()` insight. The funnel median is the independent cross-check, not the source of truth. Note also PostHog rewrites event timestamps for clock skew (`timestamp = now + timestamp - sent_at`) while the client `wallMs` is uncorrected, so the two will legitimately differ: declare the client number canonical and treat a >10% gap as a data-quality alarm, not a metric move.

EXPOSURE AND FLAGS. Ship every builder change behind a flag whose key equals its assumption id (`builder-a1-model-preset`), so `$feature_flag` breaks any funnel down by ledger row with no extra property. Bootstrap flags server-side (`@posthog/next` `bootstrapFlags`) — 100–500 ms of flag-evaluation latency is both a UX defect and a measurement artefact in a product whose headline metric is time-to-first-answer. When a funnel is used as an experiment metric, DROP the first step: PostHog makes the exposure event step 1 automatically, and including `builder_opened` double-counts.

VOLUME REALITY — WRITE IT INTO THE PLAN. Agora's entire international base is ~1,880 accounts with total active customers up 0.4% YoY, i.e. tens of first-agent sessions per week. PostHog's own formula (N = 16×variance/d²) puts the 24h-rollback guardrail at ~1,216 users/arm and tested-before-live at ~816/arm — unreachable. Only TTFT has any prospect of a powered flag test (~100/arm at CV 0.5, ~900 at a realistic CV 1.5 — measure the variance in wave 0 before promising anything). Everything else is staged rollout + before/after against a pre-declared baseline, plus a 20-participant moderated benchmark, which is the only instrument that can actually resolve the ~20–30% TTFT change the ledger predicts.

@posthog/next FOR studio_x_2 (Next.js App Router, currently zero PostHog wiring). Use `postHogMiddleware({ proxy: true })` (`/ingest`, survives ad blockers — ad-blocked users never emit a start event, so blocking biases TTFT DOWNWARD by dropping only the slow survivors' peers), `bootstrapFlags`, and `<PostHogPageView captureRouteTemplate />`. Its route property is `$route`, NOT ng-console's `routePattern` — map one to the other in `before_send`; do not let both exist. Pin the exact version (pre-release, API churn) and pin posthog-js `defaults` to ONE dated string with a comment — an unpinned bump silently changes pageview capture, replay duration semantics and internal-user detection mid-baseline.

THE SPEC IS COMMITTED AND CI-CHECKED. PostHog has NO ingestion-side schema enforcement (its enforcer plugin was archived 2024-07-26; malformed events are ingested with a warning, and 'Verified' is documentation not a gate). So: commit `docs/observability/tracking-plan.md` (human) plus `posthog.json` + `posthog-typed.ts` from `posthog-cli exp schema pull`, run `exp schema status` in CI and fail on drift, ban `captureRaw()` in lint, pin the CLI version (the `exp` prefix means the surface can change). Also commit `docs/observability/metric-definitions.md` with eight fields per metric — name · definition sentence · formula with numerator AND denominator named · population · window · exclusions · owner · action threshold. The exclusions line (bots, internal cids, duplicated agents, imported agents, resumed sessions, `trigger='auto'`) is the one every draft omits and the one that makes two people compute two different TTFTs in week one.
identity: ng-console already solves identity and it is NOT anonymous: `facade.ts identify()` calls `posthog.identify(accountUid ?? userId, sanitized(identity))` then `posthog.group('cid', cid)`, and `AuthenticatedObservabilityGate` renders NOTHING until identify has resolved — so no builder event can ever fire before identity is attached. Do not invent a second identity path in studio_x_2; call the same facade.
PERSON = `accountUid ?? userId`. This is the randomisation unit for every experiment and the unit for retention/lifecycle insights (PostHog does not support group types on lifecycle or user-paths).

ORGANIZATION = the EXISTING `cid` group type. Keep it. It is the right unit for a B2B console where two engineers share one agent, and it is what makes 'how fast is our platform' answerable per company rather than per browser.

PROJECT = a SECOND group type, `project`. Call `posthog.group('project', projectId, { name, region, createdAt })` in the SAME tick as `identify()` and `group('cid')`, before any builder event — groups only attach to events sent AFTER the call, so a late call leaves the first event of every session ungrouped. A group needs at least one property to appear in the People & groups tab.

AGENT = a THIRD group type, `agent`, but GATE IT. PostHog allows 5 group types per project; retention by agent (the per-agent AR7 the KPI doc wants) requires group analytics. Ship `posthog.group('agent', agentId, …)` behind one env-gated helper and ALWAYS send `agentId` as a plain event property regardless, so the person-level version works on day one and the switch is a config change later.

BILLING WARNING TO RAISE WITH THE OWNER BEFORE ENABLING ANY NEW GROUP TYPE: the group-analytics add-on is ~$0.000071/event and bills EVERY identified event in the project, not just events carrying group properties — roughly 2.4× the $0.00005 base identified rate. Because ng-console identifies before first render, 100% of console events are identified. Budget it as a wave-3 decision tied to AR7, not a wave-0 default; until then `cid` and `projectId` ride as event properties on the launch dashboard.

ACTIVATION IS DEFINED TWICE, ON PURPOSE. (a) A person property `activationState` ∈ none | tested | deployed | proven, written with `$set` at each milestone — instant, and the ONLY form that can target a feature flag (PostHog refuses dynamic cohorts with behavioural/lifecycle criteria as flag targets). (b) A dynamic cohort for analysis. Dynamic cohorts recalculate once per 24 h, so never use one for a same-day read or the daily design-agent report.

INTERNAL TRAFFIC: keep it, never exclude it globally, and always break down by `trafficType`. ng-console auto-classifies any @agora.io email as internal, so the design team dogfooding will otherwise flatter every median. Two required fixes: (1) pass `classifyNonProductionAsTest: true` at `AuthenticatedObservabilityGate` before the redesign hits a Vercel preview — today preview/local traffic falls through to `authenticated_identity` and is counted as EXTERNAL; (2) turn OFF PostHog's project setting 'enable the internal-user filter on all new insights', because the default is not neutral and once `defaults >= 2026-01-30` is pinned, localhost is auto-flagged internal.

PRIMARY BREAKDOWN ON EVERY BUILDER INSIGHT is `isFirstAgent`. Agora's revenue is expansion-led (Q2 2026: revenue +18% YoY, DBNRR 104%, active customers +0.4%), so a metric counting only first agents from new accounts measures the thinnest part of the business. Split Weekly Proven Agents into a new-account series and an existing-account series and report both.

insights.answers: How many people who wanted an agent got one eventually, and how many sittings it took. Guards against scoring the ~40% of interrupted tasks that resume later as abandonment.

Break down by channel and by blockedOn so carrier/regulatory waits (Twilio bundles: up to 3 business days, 21 in KYC countries) are visible as their own band rather than contaminating the builder's clock.
insights.answers: How long to a live agent, and how much of that time the builder actually controls.

No tile-level date range (a tile's own date_from silently overrides the dashboard picker and will invalidate the wave-0-vs-wave-1 comparison). Report BOTH conditional (of those who started the step) and unconditional (of all who entered the builder) rates at each step — PostHog gives conditional for free and unconditional only if you ask.
insights.answers: Where the cold-start path loses people across its 7 clicks.

Read it only next to an over-budget dwell row.

insights.spec: stack_preset_changed WHERE isDefault=false, voice_selected, opening_configured — each over builder_opened. insights.spec: deployment_went_live WHERE testedBefore=true, over all deployment_went_live, with suiteRun as a third series. insights.name: Trusted Change Rate / rollback
insights.spec: deployments surviving 24 h without deployment_rolled_back, by versionId; plus deployment_rolled_back broken down by trigger and msSinceDeploy. Declared as a DETERIORATION metric (inferiority test, no acceptable margin), not a guardrail. Powering it to detect 5%→7.5% needs ~1,216 users/arm, which is unreachable — so it is monitored with a stopping rule ('halt if it crosses 8% at any read'), never a powered test.
