critique.biggestFlaw: The north star is defined as uncomputable-by-design and the plan never schedules the work that would make it computable. FPA requires (a) a "verified first answer... anchored on the runtime's first turn-finished for that agent (server-side)" and (b) "a production session for A with turnCount >= 2". Neither exists and neither is a front-end job. I checked: `grep -rln posthog src/` in ng-console returns only files under `src/lib/observability/` — PostHog is browser-only, there is zero server-side capture, and `src/server/agent-bff-observability.ts` is a Sentry/request-id wrapper with no event emission. The `parseTurnFinishedMessage` the proposal repeatedly cites as the server anchor is consumed at `src/conversational-ai-api/index.ts:916` inside `handleRtcTranscriptPayload` — a browser RTC stream-message handler. `turnCount` appears nowhere in ng-console except an i18n plural string. So the north star's numerator, its 14-day proof qualifier, `first_live_call_received`, and Guardrail 7 (the quality test that is supposed to invalidate the week's read) all depend on an emitter that does not exist, is owned by no one in the plan, and appears in no wave. Guardrail 7 is worse than absent: as specified it compares a client event to another client event, so it will silently report ~100% agreement and certify bad data as good. Everything downstream — the FPA target, FPR, the W0 baseline, the Twyman's-law pre-registration — is built on that. The fix is to stop calling anything server-anchored until a server emitter is funded: either add a named backend workstream (Agora notification events 102/110/112/201/202 → a server-side PostHog capture or a BFF endpoint) with an owner and a wave, or redefine FPA v1 on client evidence only and label the whole system provisional until the anchor lands.

issues.issue: The "server-anchored" stop event does not exist. The proposal asserts the runtime's first turn-finished is "already parsed in src/lib/latency-metrics.ts" and can anchor the canonical stop server-side. It is parsed in the browser: parseTurnFinishedMessage is called only from src/conversational-ai-api/index.ts:916 inside handleRtcTranscriptPayload, an RTC stream-message handler, and from a test. ng-console has no server-side PostHog at all (posthog imports exist only under src/lib/observability/). Guardrail 7 therefore compares a client event against another client event and will report near-perfect agreement regardless of actual loss — certifying the exact telemetry-loss bias it was written to catch.
issues.fix: Delete the word "server-anchored" from the north star, i1, i2, the funnel and B12 until an emitter exists. Add a wave-0 backlog row with a named runtime/backend owner: receive Agora notification events 112 (turn.finished) and 201/202 (call state) on a BFF webhook route (src/routes/-webhooks.* already exists as a pattern), capture them to PostHog server-side keyed on agentId + accountUid. Until that lands, define FPA v1 on the client event, publish the client/server gap as UNKNOWN rather than as a passing quality test, and do not gate the weekly read on a check that cannot fail.

issues.issue: The tree and the event spec define the same clock three different ways, so two people implementing from the two documents get different numbers — the precise failure the "eight fields" rule exists to prevent. Name: tree calls it TTFA; the event spec mandates renaming it TTFT and says the rename is a five-minute fix that becomes unfixable later, then the tree and funnel keep saying TTFA throughout. Start event: tree i1 starts at operation_started{agent_create}; event spec starts at builder_opened. Ceiling: tree winsorizes at 900,000ms and says 900s "deliberately replaces the earlier 600s ceiling"; the event spec says "Winsorize at 600 000 ms". TTFD has the same split — tree i3 re-anchors on agent_create, event spec says "the SAME builder_opened origin".
issues.fix: Pick one name (TTFT), one start event (builder_opened — it is the only one that exists on both the blank-draft and import paths), one ceiling (900s, and state the 600s figure is retired), and do a find-replace across all four documents before anything ships. Put the single canonical definition in docs/observability/metric-definitions.md and make every other mention a link, not a restatement.

issues.issue: The north star's two targets are arithmetically inconsistent with its own baseline. FPA >= 15/week AND Fast-Proven Rate >= 45% implies a qualifying denominator of 15/0.45 = 33.3 agents per week. The same document estimates roughly 30-40 new agents per week company-wide BEFORE the stated exclusions (internal, test, duplicate, agt_default, demo agents, auto-triggered sessions, sessions failing the telemetry check) and before splitting new-account from existing-account series, which the definition requires and forbids summing. Hitting both targets requires essentially 100% of all agents created anywhere at Agora to be external, non-duplicate, qualifying first agents — while the same doc says new-logo growth is +0.4% YoY.
issues.fix: Drop the absolute count target. Set the goal on FPR only (the half design owns and the doc already says so), report FPA as an observed count with no target, and add the denominator series to the dashboard so the exclusion cost is visible. If the owner insists on a count, derive it from FPR x an observed denominator after the W0 baseline closes, not before.

issues.issue: The FPA anti-gaming guard is already defeated by a shipped feature, and the "real production conversation" leg has no caller-identity test. `configured = a voice is set and systemPrompt is non-empty` is satisfied in ONE click by seedFromVoice, which fills name, systemPrompt and greeting automatically the moment a voice is picked — the proposal documents this itself as lever l1.4. So `configured=true` proves a voice was chosen, not that anything was configured, and the fastest path to a qualifying FPA is to make voice-pick the first and only action. Separately, nothing in the production-session definition excludes the builder calling their own agent, or opening their own web widget — which for the widget channel is a single click with zero cost.
issues.fix: Redefine `configured` as evidence the user changed a default, not that a default exists: require systemPrompt !== the seedFromVoice default for that voice, or greeting edited, or a channel bound. Add to the production-session qualifier: the caller must not be the creating account's verified number or the creating browser's session id, and for web-widget deploys require a distinct anonymous distinct_id from the builder's. Add a monitored counter for self-call production sessions.

issues.issue: deploy_blocked{blockedReason, allReasons} will emit user-entered content and is unchartable. The spec calls the taxonomy "closed and small (9 reasons from lib/wizard-draft.ts publishBlocks)". It is not: publishBlocks returns interpolated free-text strings, e.g. `\`"${c.name}" needs a caller-ID number.\``, `\`"${c.name}" is missing its contacts CSV.\``, and one that embeds the list of missing template variables. publishBlockReason returns blocks[0].reason — the string, not a code. A PostHog breakdown by blockedReason would have unbounded cardinality and would put customer campaign names into the analytics store, and `allReasons` (pipe-joined) multiplies it.
issues.fix: Add a stable `code` field to the PublishBlock type (no_voice, no_channel, no_surface, no_number, no_prompt, batch_no_run, batch_no_number, batch_no_csv, batch_no_schedule, batch_uncovered_vars) and emit only the code plus counts. Never send `reason` or `allReasons`. Add the codes — not the reason strings — to the sanitizer allowlist, and add a lint rule banning interpolated template literals as event property values.

issues.issue: The plan violates its own stated multiplicity rule. Its traps section says verbatim: "CUT the count — four guardrails inflate the required sample by ~75% per arm via Spotify's beta* = beta/(G+1)" and the research says "Two guardrails (rollback, publish failure) is the defensible set". The proposal then ships seven guardrails. It also carries four input metrics, fifteen levers, fifteen assumptions, thirty-four events and fourteen insights for a product the same document says sees tens of first agents per week. The self-awareness is used as a disclaimer rather than as a cut.
issues.fix: Cut to two deterioration metrics (24h rollback/disable, first-publish failure) and one guardrail (evidence-before-live). Move runtime latency to the runtime team's own dashboard — it is not a builder guardrail and no builder change can move it. Move the SEQ survey to a research instrument with no threshold. Fold external-share and telemetry-agreement into the Data Quality insight where they belong, not the ship decision. Cut wave 0 events from 34 to the ~12 the four funnel steps actually need.

issues.issue: The north star says a guardrail breach "escalates to the named owner of that guardrail... which presupposes every row below has one - they do." No guardrail row has an owner field. Every tree row and lever has an `owner`; all seven guardrails have name/definition/threshold/why and nothing else. The document's own vanity-metric test (Cutler: a metric with no owner and no action threshold is a vanity metric by definition) fails on its most important rows.
issues.fix: Add an `owner` and an `actionOnBreach` field to all seven guardrail rows before review, and name a human, not a role, for each. If a guardrail cannot be assigned to someone who can act on it, delete it rather than shipping it unowned.

issues.issue: Guardrail 4 commits the exact measurement error it was written to correct. It says "Reported as OUR measured caller-perceived number" and then benchmarks p50 <= 900ms / p95 <= 1500ms against Openbenchmarks caller-to-caller medians of 1,296-1,740ms. But its source is e2eLatencyMs from the runtime's turn-finished payload, which is the runtime's own end-to-end figure and excludes the carrier leg, the device playout and the caller-side audio path. This is the same server-side-vs-caller-perceived mixing the guardrail accuses the existing KPI doc of doing with Retell's 680ms. The target is also set ~30% below the best measured competitor on a number Agora has never measured.
issues.fix: Rename the metric runtimeTurnLatencyMs and state plainly that it is runtime-measured, not caller-perceived. Do not print it next to Openbenchmarks figures. Set the threshold from Agora's own first four weeks of observed data, not from a competitor table. If a caller-perceived number is wanted, it requires a separate instrumented dial-in harness — scope that as its own row with its own owner.

issues.issue: The same change has two different predicted effect sizes in two parts of the same proposal, and the stated discount rule is applied inconsistently. B1 (preset slider) predicts "-60s to -105s" undiscounted, then "-20s to -35s" after the 0.33 prior — arithmetically correct. Tree row l1.1, the same change, predicts "-30 to -60s median TTFA" undiscounted and then says it should be "discounted by a 0.33 prior" — which would give -10 to -20s, not the -20 to -35s B1 states. Meanwhile l1.3 and B8 apply zero discount to predictions drawn from the same Kivetz citation.
issues.fix: Delete the effect prediction from either the tree or the ledger — keep it in exactly one place (the ledger) and have the tree reference the assumption id. Apply the 0.33 prior uniformly to every undiscounted prediction or to none, and show both the raw and discounted figure in one column so the arithmetic is auditable.

issues.issue: The entire measurement system is first-agent-only, while the document's own evidence says the money is elsewhere. It cites Agora Q2 2026 at +18% revenue, DBNRR 104%, active customers +0.4% — expansion-led — and the research explicitly says "a north star counting first agents from new builders points at the thinnest part of the funnel". The response is a breakdown dimension (isFirstAgent) and one event (agent_edited_after_live). There is no input metric, no funnel, no lever and no target for the second agent, the returning builder, or the migrator. There is also no person-level return metric anywhere in the tree despite the research recommending a D7 metric with a 7% bar; HEART Retention is assigned to agent survival, which no published benchmark can be compared against.
issues.fix: Add a fifth input metric owned by the design lead: second-agent rate (share of accounts with >=1 proven agent that create a second agent within 28 days) with its own TTFT series, and a person-level D7 return metric beside FPA with 7% as the opening target. Report the new-account and existing-account FPA series with equal prominence, not as a footnote to the headline.

issues.issue: i4 EBL and half the confidence ladder are defined on surfaces that exist only in the unshipped prototype, which has zero analytics wiring. EBL requires >=5 scenario runs with a printed verdict and a preflight evaluated with zero blocking items. Neither the scenario suite nor the preflight exists in ng-console, the live product; studio_x_2 has both but its analytics.ts dispatch() is a console.debug stub with a TODO and no PostHog client. So EBL has a stated baseline (10-20%), a stated target (>=60%) and a named owner for a number that cannot be produced until a different codebase ships to production.
issues.fix: Mark i4, l3.1, l4.1 and l4.2 as BLOCKED ON studio_x_2 PRODUCTION with an explicit date, and remove their baselines and targets until then — a modelled baseline on a surface that does not exist reads as measurement and is not. Sequence the W0 baseline on the live console's three computable legs only (agent_create, agent_publish, agent_deployment_status_update).

issues.issue: Several predictions are extrapolated from studies measuring a different quantity on a different timescale, and two of them reuse the same citation for different metrics. B8 predicts endowed progress cuts TTFD by 15-30% (-3 to -6 minutes) and l1.3 predicts it cuts time-to-first-section-completion by 15-35%, both from Kivetz 2006 — a loyalty-card study measuring median DAYS to complete ten coffee purchases over a fortnight. Transferring a multi-week goal-gradient effect to a single-sitting counter string is not supported, and the ledger itself concedes the counter is currently a bug (isDone(4) is the literal true, isDone(5) never recomputes), so what is being predicted is a bug fix plus a relabel.
issues.fix: Split B8 into two rows: a defect fix (isDone correctness) shipped alone with no predicted effect, and a separate relabel experiment measured only on blocks_remaining at mount and time-to-first-section-completion. Drop the TTFD prediction entirely — no evidence in the pack connects a progress counter to a deployment clock.

issues.issue: Predictions that are stated as numbers but are admitted in the same row to be unmeasurable at this traffic, with no alternative instrument that can resolve them. B2 (<10% BYOK open, <2% hard exits) needs 576/arm — "unreachable". B9 (publish attempts 1.8 -> 1.1; first-publish failure 10-15% -> 5-7%) needs 624/arm — "not powerable" — and both endpoints are explicitly "assumed". B11 (+8-15pp first-test rate) needs ~619/arm and falls back to a 20-participant moderated benchmark, which gives roughly +/-20% margin of error on task TIME and far worse on a binary proportion — it cannot resolve 8pp. B15 (rollback falls 1-2pp from an assumed 5%) is unpowered by admission. B14 (10-20% anonymous-to-signup conversion) cites no source at all. Guardrail 5's SEQ non-inferiority margin of -0.3 on a 7-point scale needs roughly 350 responses/arm against an expected ~10-20 survey responses per week.
issues.fix: Replace every unpowerable point prediction with a directional claim plus a pre-declared stopping rule and the observed-N it would take ("we expect BYOK-open below 10%; at our volume this is a monitored series, reviewed at W8, with no significance test"). Delete B14's conversion figure until a comparator exists. Drop the SEQ non-inferiority margin and report the mean with its CI as a qualitative read only.

issues.issue: Quota and billing are missing entirely as a journey stage and a failure mode. The product gives 300 free minutes with the first 150 card-free (free-minutes-nudge.tsx exists in the prototype), and voice tests consume minutes. There is no refusal reason for quota exhaustion in l2.2's closed taxonomy, no guardrail on "user hit the card wall before their first verified test", and no cost counter-metric anywhere — so a TTFA win that triples test-call volume is a direct COGS increase at $0.10/min that the scorecard cannot see. The one property that touches it, freeMinutesRemaining on agent_test_started, is not on the sanitizer allowlist additions list.
issues.fix: Add quota_exhausted and payment_required to the test_refused reason taxonomy; add a guardrail 'share of first agents that hit the card nudge before their first verified test' with a hard ceiling; add minutes-consumed-per-verified-test as a monitored cost counter-metric beside TTFT so a speed win that burns the free pool is visible. Add freeMinutesRemaining and minutesConsumed to the allowlist additions.

issues.issue: i4 EBL can be driven to 100% by generating five scenarios that cannot fail and auto-running them, and nothing forbids it. The suite is console-generated (l4.1) and the threshold is a count (>=5 runs with a printed verdict), not a quality bar. The only counter-signals are a judge-override rate ceiling and a saturation nudge, both of which are inside the lever description rather than the guardrail block, and neither has an owner or a threshold on the scorecard. l4.1 also notes the suite currently contains a scenario that ALWAYS fails for a config reason (transfer defaults to false), so the first-run pass rate is floored for a reason unrelated to quality.
issues.fix: Add a discriminative-power condition to EBL: a suite counts only if at least one scenario failed on its first run, and the run was user-initiated (add initiatedBy: user|auto to agent_simulation_run and exclude auto). Move the >=98% saturation alarm and the >30% judge-override alarm out of the lever prose and onto the dashboard with named owners. Exclude or label the transfer=false scenario so pass rate is not floored by a default.

issues.issue: Four rows are assigned to owners who cannot ship them, with no dependency or sequencing recorded. l4.2 (one rubric offline and online) and l4.5 (first-24-hours panel) are owned by the Runtime/voice engineering lead; l4.3 (canary) and l2.4 (logged-out demo) by the Product owner — the latter also needs marketing-site work and an abuse quota that no one owns. i3 SBDR is owned by the Design lead but its dominant variance is Twilio's regulatory queue (up to 21 business days). The blocked_on='none' filter handles the contamination, but it then measures TTFD on a population selected on the outcome — people who already had a working number — and that selection effect is never stated.
issues.fix: Add a `dependsOn` field to every lever naming the team and the prerequisite, and move rows with a non-design owner into a separate 'requested from' list so the design tracker is not carrying work design cannot schedule. State the selection effect in i3's definition and report the blocked_on='none' share alongside the median so a shrinking eligible population cannot be read as a speed win.

issues.issue: The 900s ceiling is justified with a comparison that does not hold. The north star says 15 minutes "beats the most aggressive published end-to-end competitor claim (Retell, '15 minutes')". 900s equals 15 minutes, it does not beat it — and it compares Agora's FAILURE threshold (above which a session is counted as a loss) against a competitor's advertised TYPICAL path. A ceiling and a marketing median are not comparable quantities.
issues.fix: Keep the 900s ceiling on the Parnin & Rugaber working-block grounding, which is sound, and delete the Retell comparison from the justification. If a competitive line is wanted, compare Agora's measured median/p75 against competitor claims and label theirs as undefined marketing figures — which the research already establishes.

issues.issue: No accessibility or keyboard-path metric anywhere, in a product whose entire thesis is speed of configuration and which ships a command palette. The below-1024px gap is handled as a lever (l2.1) but never as a guardrail, so a desktop-only speed win that regresses the mobile funnel passes every gate in the system. Localisation is similarly absent: `language` is on the allowlist and the product has a Spoken Language control, but no metric segments by it, and the strategic argument (l3.2) is explicitly that non-US is where Agora leads.
issues.fix: Add viewport parity to the guardrail block, not the lever list: VTR below 1024px non-inferior within 10pp of desktop, with a named owner. Add a keyboard-only completion check to the 20-participant benchmark protocol. Segment TTFT by spoken language and by account region on the launch dashboard from day one — it costs one breakdown and it is where the differentiating story is.

missingGuardrails: Cost per verified test / minutes consumed per agent — a TTFT win that multiplies test-call volume is a direct COGS increase at $0.10/min against a 300-minute free allowance, and no metric in the system can see it

Self-call exclusion on production sessions — nothing stops the builder's own phone or their own web-widget preview satisfying the 'real production conversation of 2+ turns' proof that the entire north star rests on

Support / Concierge contact rate per new agent — named in the source research as one of the two true bounded-margin guardrails and silently dropped from the final set, removing the only external signal that a faster builder is confusing people
Suite discriminative power — no rule that an eval suite must be capable of failing, so EBL can be driven to 100% with five trivially-passing auto-run scenarios
Viewport parity (VTR below 1024px within 10pp of desktop) — currently a lever, so a desktop-only speed win that regresses the mobile funnel passes every ship gate
Quota / payment-wall refusal — no reason code and no ceiling for users blocked by the 150-minute card-free limit before their first verified test
Accessibility and keyboard-path completion parity — absent entirely from a product whose headline claim is configuration speed
Survey response-rate and sampling-bias floor for the SEQ instrument — the only attitudinal signal in the plan has no guard against it becoming a self-selected trickle
Cardinality and content-safety check on event properties — no rule preventing interpolated user content (campaign names, prompt fragments) reaching PostHog, which deploy_blocked as specified would do
unsupportedPredictions: B8: endowed progress cuts TTFD 15-30% (-3 to -6 minutes) — extrapolated from Kivetz 2006, which measured median DAYS to complete ten loyalty-card purchases; no evidence links a progress counter to a deployment clock, and the change is confounded with fixing the counter's existing bug
l1.3: -15 to -35% on time to first section completion — same Kivetz citation reused for a different metric, and unlike l1.1 it is not discounted by the plan's own 0.33 prior

l1.1 vs B1: the same preset-slider change is predicted at -30 to -60s in the tree and -60 to -105s in the ledger; the tree's discounted figure would be -10 to -20s, not the -20 to -35s the ledger states

B9 / l3.1: publish attempts fall from 1.8 to <=1.1 and first-publish failure halves from 10-15% to 5-7% — all four endpoints are explicitly 'assumed', the baseline event does not exist in either codebase, and the row admits it needs 624 users/arm

B11: +8-15pp first-test rate from reordering the rail — needs ~619/arm by the plan's own formula, and the stated fallback (a 20-participant moderated benchmark) cannot resolve an 8pp change in a binary rate
B2: BYOK opened by <10% of first agents and hard exits under 2% of sessions — needs 576/arm, conceded unreachable, stated as a numeric prediction anyway
B14: 10-20% of anonymous listeners convert to signup — no source, no comparator; the cited analogues (Bland, LiveKit) publish no conversion data
B15: 24h rollback falls 1-2pp from an assumed 5% baseline, and canary adopted on >=40% of first deploys — baseline invented, metric unpowered by admission, adoption figure uncited
Guardrail 5: SEQ mean >=5.5/7 non-inferior within -0.3 — detecting 0.3 on a 7-point scale needs roughly 350 responses per arm against an expected 10-20 responses per week at this traffic

Guardrail 4: runtime p50 <=900ms / p95 <=1500ms — set ~30% below the best independently measured competitor on a quantity (caller-perceived latency) that the cited data source (runtime e2e_latency_ms) does not measure

B4: backup attach 15% -> 30-40% — measurable only within the sheet-opener population, which lever l1.1 is simultaneously targeting to shrink below 30%; succeeding at B1 makes B4 unreadable, and the conflict is not named
North star: FPA >= 15/week AND FPR >= 45% — jointly require a qualifying denominator of ~33 agents/week against an estimated 30-40 new agents/week company-wide before every stated exclusion
